w: a built ring round its star, Alma's broadcast house: studio cities on the floor, anchors' towers on the rim walls
s: a pearl-white loop round a pale star, warm seas on the floor, lit towers climbing the walls
m: none (a built ring round its star)
pop: 4 billion hands, mostly Staff grade, along the loop
lore: Alma built this ring as its broadcast house, and every news broadcast in the Hand goes out from here, eight hours late, so Praevisio can check it first. The anchors live in towers on the rim walls above the studios and are never filmed off camera.

w: city-world covering the whole surface, climate engineered
s: solid gold-and-white grid of lights, no dark side, girdled by an orbital ring and four elevator cables
m: four small moons, one hollowed into an archive
r: administration, debt records, the Board's courts
lore: The capital, named for the document that put the Republic into receivership. Every hand in the galaxy owes its debt to an office here, and the Chair has not been seen in its towers for thirty years.

w: the Board's ring round a fusion lamp: parkland and bamboo forest on the floor, schools on the rim terraces, staff in the hull decks
s: a green loop round a lamp of light, white roads across the floor, lit terraces on the walls
m: none (a built ring round a fusion lamp)
pop: 90 million hands, mostly Contract staff, and 40,000 Board children
lore: The Board built this ring to raise its children, the one childhood the Hand pays for. Forty thousand Board children are taught on the rim terraces above the parkland; the Contract staff who raise them live in the hull decks and were never schooled themselves.

w: gas giant; Continuity's inspection ring circles it, with barracks platforms hung below on cables in the cloud tops
s: tan and dusty grey bands, circled by a lit inspection ring
pop: 600 million hands, half of them Continuity staff, on the ring and its hanging platforms
lore: Continuity's watch post on the Long Haul approach to Charter. Every ship bound for the capital is stopped and searched at the ring, and the queue in orbit can last a week. Pacifiers sell places in it.

w: cold world of ice-capped mountains and cold oceans; the stamping halls are cut into the glaciers
s: dark blue seas, white peaks, cities like grey lichen
lore: Every death certificate in the Hand is stamped here, by hand, with the Board's seal, in halls cut into the glaciers. The stamping halls run day and night; in a war year they hire.

w: cold snowy world, long winters
s: white with streaks of pale blue ice
pop: 55 million hands, Staff and Contract grade
lore: Alma's healing gel is compounded here, in cold vats under the snow. The plant workers cannot afford a jar of what they make, and their burns are treated with the cheap copy from Ilha Verde.

w: rocky world-city at the crossing of two trade lanes, crusted with trading towers and docks
s: grey-brown under a crust of towers and docks, lit end to end, one large moon
lore: The debt exchange. Birth Debts are bought, bundled into tranches and sold to Continuity on a trading floor the size of a continent. A hand's whole life can change owners three times in one afternoon.

w: gas giant; the merchant houses' walled towns hang on great rotors in the cloud tops
s: soft green and fawn bands with long white cloud streaks
pop: 300 million people, old merchant families and their crews
lore: Merchant families on the Charter Road whose walled towns hang on rotors in the cloud tops. They signed their own charter a week before the Receivership and have waved it at every Hand inspector since. They pay Lode's tolls on time and nothing else.

w: temperate forest world, server halls buried beneath
s: deep green almost to the poles, few cities
lore: Praevisio keeps the forests standing because the trees cool the server halls buried beneath them. Foresters are paid to count every bird; nobody has been told why.

w: gas giant; the highlanders live on its cool living moon of plateaus and deep gorges
s: steel-blue and white bands, a grey-green moon of plateaus beside it
m: two moons: a cool living moon of grey-green plateaus cut by black ravines, and a small icy one
pop: 12 million highlanders on the living moon
lore: Highland settlers who fled the Republic's famines to the giant's cool moon and never came down from its plateaus. They keep goats, keep their own calendar, and shoot at survey drones.

w: hot volcanic world, acid rain from the smelter fumes
s: mustard yellow under a haze
pop: 400 million hands, Indentured miners, under glass roofs
lore: Lode's antimony smelters, built over the vents. The fumes turned the rain sour a century ago, and the company town lives under glass roofs the hands must scrub by hand every week, because the acid eats the cleaning machines.

w: hot world of mangrove islands and shallow sea
s: turquoise shallows broken by dark green islands
lore: Mangrove islanders who build their villages on stilts and move them each season with the tide. They hide Runners in the roots for a fee, and turn them in for a bigger one.

w: gas giant; the free university's halls float in the calm eye of a storm that never moves
s: cream and slate-blue bands round one vast white storm
pop: 3.5 billion people in the storm-eye halls, a third of them students
lore: A free university older than the Hand, its halls afloat in the calm eye of a storm that has not moved in four centuries, open to anyone who can reach it. Praevisio has offered three times to buy its library, and the faculty has voted no by a narrower margin each time.

w: cold world of long rivers and pine, its valleys slowly warming
s: white uplands, dark green valleys threaded with silver river
lore: A cold river world settled by refugees from the Republic's last famine, who have spent a century warming its valleys with black-dust fields and greenhouse vents. Its fishermen still set an empty place at every feast for those who never arrived.

w: gas giant; its valley settlers live on a living moon of deep river valleys
s: pale gold and white bands, a green moon streaked with white valley spray
m: one living moon of deep green valleys
lore: Fifty thousand people live in one long valley of waterfalls on the giant's living moon. Lode has surveyed it twice for a dam that would drown them all; the third survey team never left.

w: hot rain forest world
s: dark green under constant storms
m: one black moon used as a prison
lore: Continuity's training ground. Tranches learn jungle fighting in the rain forest below, and the moon above holds the ones who refused.

w: gas giant where the Long Haul crosses the Charter Road; Lode's refinery decks hold their height on engines that burn the gas they skim
s: rust-orange bands, two plated toll stations in close orbit
m: no natural moons; two captured rocks plated over as toll stations
pop: 900 million hands, mostly Staff grade, on the refinery decks and toll stations
lore: Lode's toll station where the Long Haul crosses the Charter Road. A thousand freighters a day pay here and fill up with gas from the refinery decks below; the founding manager named it after fool's gold as a joke that nobody now tells.

w: cold volcanic mountain world; lava vents feed the forges
s: black peaks streaked with orange furnace light
lore: Mordant's oldest forge, where hull plate is hammered in mountain foundries. Yard families have worked the same anvil line for nine generations and are buried in its slag heaps.

w: temperate farm world
s: patchwork green and gold with grey-blue seas
lore: A quiet farming world of hedged fields and stone villages. Its farmers sell grain to the Hand and children to nobody, and Alma's recruiters have learned not to visit.

w: volcanic world of black lava plains and ash; the port stands on one old shield of rock that has not flowed in a century
s: black and dark grey with orange cracks and plumes of grey ash
pop: 30 million islanders and dock crews in sealed port towns
lore: A free port built on the one old shield of rock that has not flowed in a century, its docks sealed against the ash. When the mountain wakes, the harbour shuts and every ship in port, Hand or Runner, waits out the ash together.

w: dry steppe world locked to its star; seven deep wells in the twilight band draw on ice melt seeping from the night side
s: beige and ochre twilight steppe with scattered green oases, a burnt face and a white night side
lore: Seven deep wells in the twilight tap the meltwater that seeps out from under the night side's ice, and every town lives off them; the day side is grazed at its edge and left to burn beyond. Each well has its own family that owns it. The Hand taxes the water; the families decide who drinks.

w: dry grassland steppe world
s: gold and pale green, almost no clouds
lore: Horse herders on an endless dry grass plain who refused to be counted. When Praevisio sent census drones, they shot them down and hammered the casings into horseshoes.

w: hot city-world, thick air, breath masks advised
s: brown haze over orange city lights
lore: The best hyperdrives outside Mordant's yards are built here in hot, smoky engine halls. The engine guild sells to the Hand, the Runners and the Collective, and swears the drives are identical.

w: warm farm world of wide plains, broken into grain fields by Lode's contract terraformers
s: golden plains with green river margins
lore: Lode's contract crews turned dry scrub into wide grain plains a century ago and billed the settlers for every river they moved. Lode sets the price before the harvest and collects after it. The farmers own their land and owe on their seed.

w: cold ocean world with rocky coasts
s: slate-grey seas, white coasts
lore: A cold fishing world where the fleets go out together and come back together. A captain who leaves a boat behind is never allowed to sail again.

w: arid desert world of drained seabeds; holdouts are planting salt-trees back across the old sea floors
s: pale tan and white salt flats with thin threads of grey-green in the basins
m: three small moons: a cratered rock and two captured lumps
lore: Seven hundred million people lived here until Lode drained the aquifers. Seven thousand remain, planting salt-trees across the dry seabeds, and the grey-green threads now show from orbit. The rest were relocated, the files say.

w: warm world of deep valleys and hills
s: green folds and grassy uplands
lore: Deep valleys of rainforest and grassland, settled by families who still farm the terraces their ancestors cut. Lode wants the timber; the valleys want to be left alone and have so far been ignored.

w: hot tropical world, reefs and jungle islands
s: bright turquoise and emerald
m: three moons: a smooth ice moon, a cratered rock and a captured lump
lore: Reef resorts run by old hotel families who serve anyone who pays, including Executives on leave and Runner captains. Alma has offered to buy every hotel; the families raise their prices each time.

w: barren desert and mountain world locked to its star; the robot works run along the twilight band
s: pale sand twilight with white factory grids, a white-hot face and a dark one
m: two moons: an industrial moon and a cratered rock
lore: Praevisio's repair works: broken Proxies come back from every front to be rebuilt in the twilight halls and sent out again. Solar fields cover the day side; scrap waits in the night side's cold yards. The Tranches who ship them have painted a word on the factory wall so often that Continuity no longer bothers to clean it off.

w: blue-grey gas giant; Continuity's guard stations ride its air on thermal lift, and twenty-eight prison moons circle it
s: green-blue bands, circled by grey moons
m: twenty-eight small moons, all prisons; the five biggest drawn, the largest a basalt quarry
pop: 10 billion hands in the guard stations and on the moons, a fifth of them prisoners
lore: Twenty-eight moons, each one a labour prison, numbered and never named. Prisoner hands break basalt on the largest for Charter's roads, while their guards live above the giant's clouds in stations kept aloft by its own warm updrafts.

w: barren world under ash and slag, red seams still glowing; a Grower cell is planting under the ash
s: grey and black, with dull red streaks and a few faint green valleys
pop: 2 million hands in roofed slag towns and a few hundred Growers
lore: Once lush, now Lode's slag dump, its seams still glowing. Lode filed it as fully reclaimed twelve years ago, and the hands live under ash roofs. A small Grower cell has been quietly planting under the ash ever since; a few valleys now show green from orbit.

w: dry rocky world locked to its star, thin soil, hill farms along the twilight band
s: brown and grey twilight crossed by fine lines of wall, a bare scorched face and a dark one
lore: Dry hill farmers in the twilight who pick stones out of their fields every spring and build walls with them; the stone is quarried on the day side, the water hauled in from the night side's ice. The walls are older than the Hand and the farmers will tell you so.

w: temperate world of rolling hills
s: soft green under thin clouds
m: three moons: a cratered rock, a smooth ice moon and a captured lump
lore: Alma's showcase holding: rolling hills where every advertisement is filmed. The happy families on screen are hired by the hour, and tourists are not allowed past the coast.

w: Praevisio's compute shell: three nested shells of plates round a star, each living on the waste heat of the one inside, a Matrioshka brain running the forecast engines
s: a closed sphere of dark plates with cold white lights, warm glow showing through a few open plates
m: none (a built shell round its star)
pop: 2 billion hands in sealed towers on the plates
lore: Three shells of thinking plate round a captured star, each run on the heat the one inside throws away. Two billion hands check the forecast engines' work from sealed towers on the outer plates. Nobody leaves without a suit, and nobody gets a suit without a forecast.

w: cold ammonia gas giant; one refinery rig, held aloft on its own lift engines, works the upper cloud
s: pale yellow with brown bands
r: fuel gas, ammonia, black market goods
pop: 20,000 Runners and a handful of Nhal exiles, on the rig and in the skimmers
lore: An ammonia giant where Runner gas skimmers fill their tanks away from Lode's meters, diving from a refinery rig that hangs on its own engines and falls if they stop. A few Nhal exiles run that rig, the best on the lane, and charge humans double.

w: temperate world of forests and industrial coasts, an orbital ring of slipways above the equator
s: blue and green, its coasts lined with yellow-lit docks, a steel orbital ring of slipways round its waist
m: three moons: two grey cratered rocks, and a third plated over as a dry dock
lore: Mordant's capital-ship yard. Every Mandate's keel is laid on the orbital ring above the coast, and the lifers who build them are buried in the hulls they finish.

w: airless iron world, its plains cut into stepped red pits
s: dark red and black, the pits lit along their terraces
pop: 150 million hands, Indentured miners, in sealed pit towns
lore: An airless iron world that exists only to feed Classis's yards. The miners live in sealed towns cut into the pit walls. Ore trains run straight from the pits to the launch rails, and so do the miners' shifts.

w: dead world of slag plains under thin poisoned air, deep mine galleries below
s: brown and grey under a dirty haze, scored with launch rails
pop: 1.6 billion hands in the old mine galleries
lore: The surface died of slag a century ago, and the yard crews moved down into the old mine galleries. They come up only at shift change, to the launch rails, and some children have never seen the sky.

w: ocean world of small white marble islands
s: deep blue scattered with white islands, the quarry cuts bright on their hills
lore: Island quarries cut white marble for Charter's facades. The islanders say the Board walks on their hills; they mean it as a curse.

w: temperate world of forests and lakes, the larger half of a double planet
s: green and gold, its brown-green marsh twin hanging close
m: a twin planet, Bina Minor, a marsh world hanging close
lore: The larger half of a double planet. Its golden timber panels every Board office in the Hand, and its foresters cannot afford a chair made of it.

w: temperate farm world of deep wind-blown soil, plains and forests, laid down by Lode
s: yellow-brown plains, green hills
lore: A century ago Lode blew ground rock across a bare world until the dust lay deep enough to farm. It is now the richest farm world in the sector; Lode ships its harvests to Charter and rations the farmers' own bread.

w: city-world of yards and barracks
s: grey grid, hazard-yellow docks at the poles
pop: 60 billion hands, mostly Indentured yard crews
lore: Sixty billion yard hands live in barracks blocks laid out like one endless army camp. The shift sirens are so loud they can be heard from orbit, people say.

w: warm hill world, terraced and greened by Alma
s: green terraces, soft white cloud
lore: Alma greened these bare hills for its Executives: tea terraces and rest houses where they come to recover from their work. The pickers sing on Alma's orders; silence on the slopes is reported.

w: world-city of silver cities, canyons and lake plateaus
s: blue lakes and tan canyons between silver cities
lore: Twenty billion people under their own elected assembly: the biggest world the Hand never acquired. Lode tolls every ship that leaves, and the assembly pays rather than fight.

w: ocean world, cold deep seas, almost no land
s: dark navy blue, almost no land
pop: 200 million hands, divers and technicians, in pressure towns on the seabed
lore: Praevisio's cold vaults lie on the seabed, cooled by black water, with the technicians in pressure towns beside them. Divers who repair the vaults are paid well and forecast to die young.

w: slate-blue gas giant; its living moon holds empty forests, grassland and stone rings
s: a slate-blue giant, and beside it a green and blue moon with no city lights
m: two moons: a living moon of empty forest and grassland, and a small dark rock
pop: uninhabited; a few hundred pilgrims on the moon at any time
lore: Empty forests and stone rings on the giant's moon, older than anyone can date. The Unwritten say the first war against thinking machines ended here, and pilgrims land illegally to leave broken circuit boards on the stones.

w: dry tidally locked world; plains in the twilight band packed with barracks
s: a dusty brown twilight ring with long rows of barracks, a burnt day face, a frozen night face
pop: 400 million hands, most of them Tranche soldiers
lore: A Tranche depot in the twilight band. Regiments are raised here from debts bought at Cambium, issued fatigues and wrist counters, and shipped out within a month. Solar fields on the day side power the depot; the night side's ice is cut for water, and its cold is used to store the dead.

w: hot desert of salt flats
s: dazzling white with brown edges
lore: A salt-flat world where Runner crews land on the hard pan because no Hand patrol can tell one track from another. The salt diggers ask no questions and sell water by the cup.

w: cold city-world of forests and mountains
s: silver city grid with dark forests and snowy peaks
lore: Thirty billion people behind walls of cold storage. Its freezing cartels will store anything for anyone, and Repossessors bring them debtors in sealed crates to keep until the price is right.

w: warm dry world of dense thorn brush
s: olive and khaki scrub
lore: Dense thorn brush covers everything, and the settlers who live in it cut their roads anew every year. Runner crews pay well for a guide.

w: warm airless world of bauxite pits; the towns are sealed under domes
s: brick red and pale tan, scarred with pits
pop: 700 million hands, Indentured, in domed pit towns
lore: Lode's alum and bauxite pits on an airless rock. The red mud from the mines piles against the town domes and gets into the air locks and the lungs, and the hands joke they were born rust-coloured.

w: temperate world of forests around bright inland seas
s: green land around bright inland seas
lore: Gem dredgers work the inland seas for the stones Executives wear. A diver who finds a stone above a set size gets one day off; most never see it.

w: warm world of mud flats, marsh and slow brown rivers
s: brown and green, its twin looming close
m: a twin planet, Bina Major, and three small moons
lore: The smaller half of the double planet. Mud-flat farms feed Bina Major's foresters, and the two worlds have quarrelled over water rights since before the Hand.

w: cold world of tundra and glaciers, its lowlands being warmed by Alma
s: white tundra with spreading green lowlands and open grey-blue sea
pop: 2.1 billion hands, clinic staff and mothers, in domed clinic cities
lore: Alma's birth clinic for the sector, under domes on a tundra Alma is warming one valley at a time. Most hands in this sector were born here, and each left with a bill. The maternity wards play soft music all day; the billing floors play none.

w: mild city-world; a ring of ledger vaults circles the equator
s: grey and white city grid under a bright orbital ring
lore: The Board's treasury, where every toll, tax and interest payment is booked. Its towers and the ring above them hold no money at all, only ledgers, and the ledgers are guarded like vaults.

w: cool airless industrial world; the shield works sit under domes
s: steel grey with orange furnace dots
m: one white moon, half shot away
pop: 2.5 billion hands, mostly Contract, under domes and in buried halls
lore: Mordant's shield works: every Mandate's deflector generators are built here under domes and proof-tested by firing on them from the single white moon, which has been shot half away by the misses.

w: cool city-world under thin cloud
s: grey cities under thin cloud
lore: A cool city-world of arms makers that votes every year on joining the Hand. It has voted no by one percent for forty years, and Alma spends heavily on the campaign.

w: temperate city-world of long white halls
s: bright white cities on dark ground
lore: Every Gleaner lens is ground here, in long white halls. The grinders are proud of their work and do not ask where the drones go.

w: dry industrial world of factory towns
s: grey-tan under yellow smog
lore: Factory towns that make cheap copies of Alma's happiness pill and sell them across the Core. Alma calls it theft; the buyers call it the only way to afford feeling fine.

w: a built ring round its star: Lode's freight ring on the Long Haul, its floor plains, seas and docker towns
s: a rust-orange band round a white star, freight piers bristling from its outer hull
m: none (a built ring round its star)
pop: 4 billion hands, mostly Contract dockers, on the ring floor
lore: Lode built this freight ring when its depot on the Long Haul outgrew any planet. Cargo changes hulls at the piers on the outer hull and hands change contracts on the floor below. The dockers strike more often than anywhere else in the sector, and a Local runs the strike fund.

w: small airless rocky world inside a dense asteroid belt, girdled by an orbital ring of slipways
s: a grey cratered world with a ring of slipways round its equator, inside a belt of grey rocks lit by yellow yard lamps
m: none; a dense asteroid belt circles it
pop: 40 million hands, yard crews in the rocks and the yard towns below
lore: Mordant's inner rim yards: a ring of slipways round the equator, built inside an asteroid belt so the ore is already in orbit. Yard crews live in the rocks they mine, hollowing each one from the inside until it cracks.

w: cold ice world being warmed; a dark forest belt spreads along the equator
s: white ice with a dark green belt of forest and grey open water at the equator
pop: 30 million hands, most of them prisoners
lore: A labour camp on a cold world Continuity is warming for its timber. Defaulters plant the forest belt and cut it until their sentence is served, and the sentence grows with every tree they miss. The belt widens each year; the sentences have kept pace.

w: cold ice world, slowly warming; birch forest creeps out from the equator
s: white with pale green birch belts and thawing grey lakes
lore: Forest villagers make paper the old way, from birch pulp, and seed the thaw line with new birch every spring as the ice draws back. The Collective buys the paper because Praevisio cannot read what was never digital.

w: barren dusty world of gypsum quarries, almost no air
s: bone white with grey quarry scars
pop: 80 million hands, Indentured, in sealed quarry towns
lore: A barren world of gypsum quarries worked from sealed domes. Its dust coats everything white and gets through every seal, and the hands call their lungs the company's eighth quarry.

w: temperate living world of forests, mountains and plains, landscaped by Alma
s: bright green with clear skies
pop: 6.5 billion hands, mostly farmers and staff
lore: Alma's rest world for Executives, reshaped from a cold steppe over ninety years until every view was right. Hands farm food for the retreats and are forbidden to enter them; guests who rest too long are separated quietly.

w: warm ocean world of jungle islands and reefs
s: emerald islands on deep blue
pop: 300 million villagers and a small Kiru exile community
lore: A warm sea world where a small Kiru ark crew settled on a reef, and the fishing villages let them stay. Hand broadcasts say the reef is empty.

w: cold pale-orange gas giant with unbreathable air; Lode bottles helium from its clouds
s: pale orange haze over faint bands
pop: 670 million hands, Contract gas crews on refinery platforms
lore: Lode bottles helium from an atmosphere no one can breathe. Crews live on refinery platforms held up by engines that burn what they skim, and work outside in sealed suits rented by the shift. A crew that tears a suit pays for the suit before the doctor.

w: cold airless rocky world with ice in its polar craters
s: dark grey with ice caps
pop: 50 million hands, mostly Pacifiers, in buried barracks
lore: Continuity's garrison guarding Ferraria's yards, its barracks buried under the dark rock against bombardment. Its soldiers outnumber the yard crews they guard, and both sides know whom they are guarding against.

w: gas giant; the free farmers live on its big temperate moon of rolling farmland
s: pale lemon and grey bands, its green and gold farming moon close beside it
m: two moons: a big farming moon, green and gold under thin cloud, and one small grey moon
pop: 210 million free farmers, all on the farming moon
lore: A quiet farm moon where Lode built every grain silo and owns them all. The farmers are free to sell to anyone else, as long as they don't mind watching the crop rot in the fields.

w: hot jungle world grown by Alma over a dry world, warm rain on schedule
s: deep emerald with white rain bands, a faint dust ring
m: two moons, and a faint ring of dust shed by the smaller
pop: 40 million hands, almost all service staff
lore: Alma grew this jungle over a dry world for tired executives: treehouse suites, warm rain on schedule, and a pill with breakfast. The staff are Indentured hands who may not be seen by guests; they move through tunnels under the canopy.

w: temperate world of sea and sheer-sided mesas
s: turquoise sea dotted with tan stone islands
r: fish, cable-ferry trade; imports food and medicine
lore: Towns sit on the tops of flat stone mesas rising from a warm sea, linked by cable ferries. The rock grows nothing, so every meal and every medicine is shipped in, and whoever controls the ferries controls the price of bread.

w: temperate grassland world, long seasons
s: bands of yellow, red and violet grass
lore: Endless grassland that turns yellow, red and violet with the seasons, home to billions of free herders and grain farmers. They pay the Hand a lane tax and nothing else, and every Board meeting someone proposes changing that.

w: warm swamp world, rising water drowning the old fields
s: brown-green marsh under heavy mist, a ring of wreckage beside it
m: three moons, one cracked in half and shedding a ring of wreckage
r: peat, methane, a toll beacon on the main lane
pop: six hands, the toll-beacon crew, in orbit
lore: Lode's climate work here went wrong two generations ago: the caps melted, the swamps rose over the settlers' fields, and the settlers left. Only a toll beacon remains, crewed by six hands on a ten-year contract, and the steeples of drowned chapels still stick up out of the water.

w: warm ocean world with scattered islands
s: bright blue with pale reef shallows
r: pearls, lacquer, shell goods, luxury goods
lore: Ocean world of pearl beds and lacquer workshops, selling luxury to the core by the shipload. The pearl divers' guild sets the price, and it has turned down three Alma offers to buy the beds and rename the sea.

w: cool dry world where fire-grown grey forests are spreading over the plains
s: grey-green with smoke smudges over tan plains
lore: The grey forests here grow back after fire faster than anywhere known, and each summer the settlers burn a district on purpose so the forest spreads a little further into the dry plains. Lode once tried to mine the ash for fertiliser; the settlers burned the survey camp too.

w: tilted world: equatorial jungle, icy poles
s: green belt with white caps that swell and shrink
r: timber, fruit, ice water for passing freighters
lore: A tilted world where the north freezes for half the year while the south steams. Whole towns are built on rails and move between hemispheres twice a year, a slow migration that takes forty days.

w: temperate world, glass beaches, forested mountains
s: blue and green with glittering white coastlines
r: glass art, high technology, warehousing, tourism
lore: Its beaches are glass, fused by ancient meteor strikes, and its craftsmen blow and cut it into art that sells across the core. Alma wants the coast for a resort; the glassmakers want to be left alone.

w: cold dry world, frozen desert and mountains, archive vaults beneath
s: white and pale grey, almost featureless
lore: Under its frozen desert lie archives older than the Receivership, including, it is said, the court's original ruling. The Board offers to buy the archives every decade. The archivists answer every decade, in writing, that they are not for sale.

w: cold world of icy tundra and deep caverns
s: white with blue crevasse lines
lore: Diamonds lie in the ice caves like gravel, and the families who cut them have kept Lode's survey ships away for a century by simply lying about the yields. Praevisio has noticed the numbers don't add up.

w: gas giant; the brokers' cities float on heat drawn up chimneys from the deep, and the farms are on its living moon
s: pale green and brown bands, a big green-blue living moon
m: two moons: a living farm moon and a small grey one
r: information, grain from the moon, fuel gas
pop: 3.5 billion, most in the floating cities, the farmers on the moon
lore: A gas giant of information brokers, whose cities float on heat drawn up from the deep and whose grain comes from its living moon. Anything can be learned for a price. Praevisio is its biggest customer and buys the Hand's own leaks back before Continuity can find them.

w: airless rocky world; roofed valleys of docks, hostels and taverns
s: grey-brown with lit dock towns along the valleys on the nightside
r: ship repair, crew services, spare parts
lore: A lane town grown into a planet: repair docks, crew hostels and taverns under pressure roofs along the main valleys. Runner crews refit here openly, because half the docks are owned by Runner families.

w: hot jungle and ocean world
s: dark green islands in a blue-black sea
lore: Jungle and ocean full of big game, kept as a hunting reserve by a free-world family that rents it to Hand executives by the week. Guides whisper that some hunts are for animals that walk on two legs.

w: airless rocky world of deep gorges and cliffs; the post is cut into the cliff faces
s: red-brown with black shadowed gorges
pop: 2 million hands, mostly Pacifiers and signals staff
lore: Continuity's listening post, cut into a hundred kilometres of cliffs. Every message that crosses the sector passes through here, and the garrison is rotated every six months so nobody stays long enough to make a friend.

w: gas giant; the settlers live on its wet highland moon
s: cream and slate bands, a big green moon veined with white water
m: one moon, a living highland moon with the great waterfall
r: hydro power, fish, wool from the moon
lore: Its people live on the moon, named for a waterfall a kilometre high, where the settlers' founding stone is carved with one line: "Nobody here owes." They have kept that promise for three hundred years by staying poor and uninteresting.

w: gas giant; garden cities on great lift cells drift with the seasons, steered by sail
s: green and pale bands, one grey moon
lore: Its garden cities ride great lift cells and steer by sail, and their clerks register births for free, with no debt attached. The Hand does not recognise the papers, but thousands of parents come anyway so that their child's first document says nothing about money.

w: violet gas giant; the vineyards and cellars are on its two living moons, warmed by the giant's glow
s: a banded violet giant with two small green and blue moons
m: two living moons, both terraced with vineyards
r: wine, luxury goods, a little fuel gas skimmed for the cellars' own ships
pop: 28 million vintners, all on the two moons
lore: Wine country on two living moons of a violet giant: terraced vineyards and deep cellars that sell bottles to the core and hide Collective cargo in the same crates. Runners pay in good wine; Growers come to learn how old vines survive thin moon soil.

w: temperate world of grassy plains and low hills, terraformed by Lode two centuries ago
s: yellow-brown plains with green river valleys under thin cloud
lore: Lode's oldest grain holding: its terraformers ground the hills into wind-blown soil a hundred metres deep, two centuries ago. Machines work it, and a few Contract hands fix the machines. The crop is weighed in orbit and the holding retains none of it.

w: mild world of low hills and meadows
s: soft green with violet flowering patches
lore: A small, quiet world of herb farms and cottage chemists who make a cheap remedy for withdrawal from Alma's pill. Dry houses all over the sector buy it, and Alma's lawyers are working on a way to call that theft.

w: dry world locked to its star; jagged mountains and dusty valleys along the twilight band, a baked day side and an ice-capped night side
s: tan and ochre twilight band with dark ridges between a scorched face and a white night cap
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a small captured lump
r: goats, minerals, water rights, night-side ice
lore: Jagged twilight valleys where every spring is fed by night-side ice, every pipe down from the dark is owned by a family, and every family keeps a rifle. The day side is nobody's but the goats'. Water feuds here outlast lives; a Hand mediator once arrived to settle them and was shot by both sides.

w: airless rocky world; the repair towns sit in valleys roofed over with pressure domes
s: grey-green rock with dark valleys and the glint of dome roofs
r: machine repair, simple robots, spare parts, ore
lore: A free world of repair shops under pressure domes in airless valleys, keeping old, simple machines running long after Praevisio stopped supporting them. The domes leak and are patched daily. The Unwritten call it a den of machines; its mechanics answer that none of theirs can think.

w: cool windy ocean world with long thin islands
s: grey-blue sea streaked with white cloud and long green islands
lore: Windswept island world where the settlers harness the gales that never stop blowing west to east. Every town is built facing east, and every door is on the sheltered side.

w: temperate world of endless fields
s: golden-brown with green strips and small blue seas
lore: Oat and barley fields from pole to pole, sold at half Lode's price to anyone who will collect. Lode's answer has been to buy up the freighters that come to collect.

w: cold upland world slowly being warmed; green pastures spreading out of the ice from the equator
s: white ice with a widening band of pale green and drifting cloud
lore: The shepherds' moots are warming this ice world a field at a time, and the upland pastures green a little further every decade. Its weather service predicts the lane storms better than Praevisio does, using sheep, barometers and old songs. Praevisio has offered to buy the method three times and been sold a ram.

w: slow-turning rocky world with a ninety-day day; the towns crawl round it on rails to stay in the twilight
s: one face blazing white, the other dark, a slow bright terminator
lore: Its day lasts ninety standard days, so the towns ride on rails, crawling west to stay in the dusk; glassworks follow the glare and salt pans freeze behind. Towns keep two clocks, one for the sun and one for the body, and a Hand inspector who lands at local noon may wait six weeks for evening.

w: tidally locked world; savannah, canyons and swamps along the twilight band
s: rust-red and olive twilight band with dark canyon cracks, a burnt day side and a white night side
lore: Red savannah, canyons and swamps run in a band between a burnt day side, where the smiths dig iron, and a frozen night. Ranchers move herds across the canyons on cable bridges. Their blades are famous; the Hand banned their export, which doubled the price.

w: pale green gas giant; the granary farms are on its large living moon
s: pale green and cream bands beside a large green-gold moon
m: one large living moon of farmland under clear skies
pop: 980 million, nearly all on the moon
lore: A rich granary on the Charter Road: farms cover its big living moon, and the grain ships load under clear skies. It sells to anyone: the Hand, the Collective, free ports. Both sides have tried to take it; both sides keep buying from it.

w: cool moorland world of peat and low hills
s: brown and purple moors under low cloud
lore: A cold, peaty world of shepherds and distillers whose spirits are drunk on every Mordant bridge. The distillers refuse to sell the recipe and Mordant officers refuse to drink anything else.

w: airless rock world; the yards and cities are domed and buried
s: bare grey-amber rock with dome lights, yard lights round its moon
m: one moon, ringed with dock frames
pop: 2 billion, under domes and in buried towns
lore: A free world of domed cities whose own small shipyards build freighters for anyone, on the rock and on the dock frames round its moon. Mordant has offered to buy the yards four times; each time the yards built something faster that year.

w: damp, warm world of fungal forests and mist
s: grey-white and mauve, misty
lore: Fungal forests where one grey mushroom yields a compound in Alma's happiness pill. Alma buys every crop and owns none of the land, and the growers have just learned what their crop is for.

w: cool blue-green gas giant; the burial mounds cover its living moon
s: teal and slate bands beside a dull green moon
m: two moons: a cool living moon of hills and mounds, and a cratered rock
pop: 8 million, all on the living moon
lore: Burial mounds a thousand years old cover the hills of its cool living moon, built by people nobody remembers. The settlers farm around them and will not dig, not even when Lode's survey said the mounds sit on iron.

w: dry airless rocky world; the gate town is buried in the rock
s: bare yellow-grey rock
lore: Lode closed its toll gate here thirty years ago. The locals kept it open from a buried town under the gate and now charge their own toll, a single small coin, spent on its upkeep. Runners pay it gladly, and drink the ale brewed below.

w: tropical world of mountains, oceans and farmland
s: green mountains, deep blue sea, rust-red mine scars
lore: Tropical mountains full of iron, a busy port and yards that build ore haulers for free worlds across the sector. Lode and Mordant both want it, and the port plays them off against each other.

w: cold airless mountain world; the barracks are buried in the rock
s: dark grey peaks with white frost in every crater
m: two moons, one cratered to dust as a live-fire range
pop: 25 million hands, mostly Tranche recruits and instructors
lore: Every Tranche number is issued here. Recruits live in barracks cut into the mountains and drill outside in pressure suits, under a wall listing the numbers that were paid in full. They are told to find a space on it.

w: temperate ocean world of green islands, terraformed by Alma
s: bright blue with green island coastlines
pop: 600 million hands, mostly clinic staff and newborns
lore: Alma made these seas beautiful and set its birth clinics on the islands. The yard crews of the next generation are born here, billed here, and shipped to the yards as soon as they can hold a tool. Nobody born here remembers the sea.

w: volcanic world of mountains and furnace valleys
s: grey mountains with orange lava and furnace glow
lore: Mordant's arms works, cut into volcanic mountains: guns for every Hand hull are forged here on lava heat and tested in the sealed valleys where the workers live. The warning sirens are on a timetable.

w: temperate world of plains and forests, heavily built up, with a slipway cable rising from the equator
s: green and gold, a bright line of slipways running up to its two yard moons
m: two moons, both plated over as yards, with a line of slipways strung between them and the planet
lore: Seat of the Mordant dynasty and its main yards, where the slipways hang in a line from the planet to its two moons like washing on a cord. Here twelve thousand yard crew downed tools in one shift and walked off; the Walkouts were born that day, and the dynasty still has the names.

w: cold gas giant of pale blue-grey bands, ringed by picket forts
s: pale blue-grey bands, a lattice of forts in orbit
pop: 5 million hands, mostly inspectors and fleet crew, in the forts and customs platforms
lore: A fortified picket world guarding the main lane into Mordant's home sector. Customs platforms hang on cables from the forts into the upper cloud, every ship entering is searched there, and the inspectors earn a bonus per fault found, so faults are always found.

w: cold gas giant of dull blue bands; a reserve fleet is parked in its orbit
s: dull grey-blue bands, a crowded orbit of dark hulls
m: three small moons: two captured rocks and one dark ice-rock
r: laid-up warships, spare parts, fuel gas
pop: 500,000 hands, mostly caretaker crews living aboard
lore: Mordant's reserve fleet sleeps here: old Mandates and Decrees parked in rows, crewed by skeleton teams who live aboard for years. One Lode gas rig rides a storm band below to keep the tanks full. In a crisis the Hand counts these ships; nobody counts how many still fly.

w: hot volcanic smelter world, one sealed city over the cooling crust
s: rust-brown under yellow haze, lava glowing in the cracks
lore: A sealed city of slag and smelters built over a volcanic crust, turning Lode's ore into Mordant's steel on the planet's own heat. Its towers are built from the waste of its furnaces, and the filtered air still tastes of iron.

w: warm gold gas giant; the orchards are on its largest moon
s: gold and amber bands with nine moons visible from orbit
m: nine moons; the largest is a warm living world of orchards and the rest are rock and ice
pop: 9 billion, nearly all on the largest moon
lore: Nine moons circle a gold giant, and the largest is a warm, rich world of orchards and old families who sell fruit to the yards and refuse to sell one hectare of land. The only free world in Mordant's home sector, and proud of it.

w: frozen world of ice oceans, plains and canyons; the prison barracks are under the ice
s: pure white with blue ice canyons
lore: An ice world where Continuity keeps the people Mordant can't fire: strike leaders, slow workers, the families of Walkouts. They live in heated barracks under the ice and cut it for the yards' coolant lines, in shifts that never end.

w: temperate world of shallow seas, tidal flats and a few low islands
s: silver tidal flats and pale blue sea
m: three moons, which drive the great tides
lore: A shallow-sea world where the tide goes out forty kilometres twice a day, leaving glittering flats of quartz sand. The tide-towns stand on stilts, make fine electronics from the sand, and have never let anyone, Hand or Collective, garrison them.

w: barren airless world of ore claims and salt pans
s: dusty orange with white salt pans and the pockmarks of a thousand claims
m: four small moons, three of them captured lumps
lore: An airless rock where anyone can stake a claim, and most do. Prospectors live in pressure huts dug into the salt, mine ore by hand and sell it to whoever's freighter lands first. Lode's offer to buy all the claims is pinned to the saloon wall.

w: cold mountain world of snowy ridges and frozen valleys
s: jagged grey with snowy ridges and white ice fields
pop: 15 million in stone halls cut into the ridges
lore: Mountain clans hold the passes from heated stone halls cut into the ridges, and charge for every crossing. They also charge Hand freighters for not being robbed, which the Hand pays and books as an operating cost.

w: pale gas giant; the old kingdom rules its living moon, a temperate jungle with white stone cities
s: a pale green-gold giant, and beside it a dark green moon flecked with white cities
m: four moons: the living jungle moon, one grey rock, one dark ice-rock and a small captured lump
r: art, timber, tribute, fuel gas skimmed under crown licence
pop: 4 million, almost all on the living moon
lore: One family has ruled the jungle moon for four hundred years and still crowns its kings in white stone cities. Royal skimmers sell the giant's gas under a crown licence. The crown pays the Hand a yearly fee to stay on, and calls the fee a gift.

w: moist world of overgrown plains and ruined cities, regrown by Growers after Lode left
s: dark green with rusty ruin patches and old pit scars greening over
m: two moons, one grey and one a small captured rock
lore: A Lode industrial world abandoned when the ore ran out. Growers moved in, reseeded the poisoned plains and let the jungle eat the factories. Forty years on, the old pit scars are green and vines hold up the smelter roofs.

w: dry plains world of scrapyards under a dusty sky
s: grey-brown, littered with glinting wrecks and cut scars
r: scrap metal, salvaged parts, rebuilt ships
lore: Old Mordant hulls come here to be broken for scrap by free crews. The Walkouts buy back the best parts, and Mordant has started cutting the guns off before it sells the wrecks.

w: blue-grey gas giant of seven moons; the breeders' halls are on the largest, a living moon of forests, valleys and snowy ranges
s: a blue-grey banded giant, and beside it a green moon of valleys between snowy ranges
m: seven moons; the largest is a living world, the rest ice and rock
lore: Its moon's mountain houses breed the horses Board families ride on their private estates, and ship them to orbit in heated stalls. A Seldwyn foal costs more than a Contract hand's whole debt, and is better fed.

w: temperate world split by a great rift valley
s: green on both sides of a long dark scar
lore: Split by a great rift valley into two nations that have not spoken in a century. Each side sells the other's secrets to the Hand.

w: hot jungle world, huge brown rivers
s: deep green with brown river veins under heavy cloud
lore: Jungle so dense no road survives a year. The settlers live in river boats, and the only map anyone trusts is the one the boat captains keep in their heads.

w: dry world of purple-red mountains, salt basins and bright exchange cities
s: purple-red rock, white salt basins, bright cities
lore: Lode's freight exchange, where the toll on every lane is set each morning. Freighter captains from across the galaxy wait in its halls for prices that decide whether their families eat.

w: cool forest world
s: dark blue-green with white steam over the vents
lore: Praevisio's data vaults lie under a cold forest, cooled by its rivers. Locals are forbidden to cut trees, light fires or speak above a whisper near the vents.

w: world of acid seas, with grey stone plateaus standing out of them
s: yellow-green seas and grey plateaus under a sour haze
m: two moons, one grey and one a small captured rock
pop: 8 million hands, mostly technicians, in pressure halls inside the plateaus
lore: Praevisio's robot factories stand on sealed stone shelves above the acid seas, building Proxies by the million. The workers live in pressure halls cut into the shelves and are paid in performance points that lose value each month.

w: tidally locked world; a twilight band being greened into rainforest and fields between a desert day side and an ice night side
s: a ring of green and tan twilight between a brown desert face and a white night face
lore: Alma's botanical gardens: the twilight band is being greened a strip at a time, and herb farms grow under domes ahead of the new soil. Mirrors on the day side drive the rain; the night side keeps the harvest frozen. The pickers get free medicine in return, which they are billed for later.

w: chalk-pale gas giant; Lode's gas rafts drift in its upper clouds
s: chalk-white bands with grey ridges of cloud
m: two moons: an ice moon mined for water, and a captured rock hollowed into the toll station
pop: 6 million hands, mostly toll staff on the station moon and raft crews
lore: A Lode toll station hollowed into a captured rock on the main lane, where freighters wait in line for days. Gas rafts drifting in the chalk-white clouds below fill their tanks, the ice moon fills their water, and the market sells water, fuel and good news, all at toll prices.

w: dry world, desert and scrub, deep old wells
s: yellow-brown with a few green oases
lore: The last free water stop before the Hand's toll lanes. Its wells are deep and old, and the water is free to anyone who pays for the bucket.

w: dry temperate steppe; long rivers run through a few green valleys
s: green-gold steppe with thin river lines
lore: Steppe and rivers, horse herds and a billion people who still move camp with the seasons. Lode has tried to fence the steppe twice; the fences are now fuel.

w: airless rock; the contract vaults are sealed under white domes
s: pale grey-green with rows of white vault domes
pop: 15 million hands, mostly Staff clerks, under the domes
lore: The Board's contract office, sealed under white domes on an airless rock: every transfer of a hand from one employer to another is countersigned here, millions a day. A hand whose papers are lost between signatures belongs to nobody for a while, and some are never found.

w: hollow airless asteroid, cold; the base is cut inside it
s: dull grey rock with a few lit hatches
pop: 68,000 Collective fighters and crew, including a few hundred Kiru
lore: A hollow asteroid fitted out as a base by Collective crews who meant to stay a week. That was nine years ago. A small Kiru exile community runs its air plant, and reminds everyone who breathes it.

w: blue-green gas giant; its cities hang under great gas cells at the breathable layer, each with a bell tower on its keel
s: blue-green bands with a pale yellow storm
pop: 700 million in some four hundred hanging cities
lore: Its cities hang beneath vast gas cells, bell towers slung under their keels. Every city rings its bells when a Hand ship enters orbit, and the sound carries through the clouds until the whole planet knows within minutes. Runners love it; the Hand finds it rude.

w: temperate archipelago world
s: blue sea with countless green islands
m: three moons: a cratered rock, a smooth ice moon and a captured lump
pop: 5 million islanders, including a small Nhal community
lore: A scatter of islands used by Runners and Collective crews to hide ships in sea caves. A small Nhal community keeps the lookout towers.

w: grey-blue gas giant; one vast stacked city hangs in its rain layer, tethered by cables to a weighted keel in the deep air
s: grey-blue bands under constant cloud, a violet storm
r: black market, information, trade, fuel gas
lore: A rain-soaked city of neon decks stacked a hundred levels high, held in the giant's wet layer by cables to a keel nobody has seen. Everything can be bought here, and anything left on a walkway is gone in an hour. Runners, Repossessors and Hand agents all keep rooms here, sometimes on the same floor.

w: dry stony world locked to its star; glasshouse fields spread along the twilight band under a sun that never sets
s: grey-brown twilight band glinting with glass and patches of green, a scorched face and a dark frozen one
lore: A stony desert world where the glasshouse families farm under a sun that never sets, and every decade the green under the glass reaches a little further into the dusk. Each glasshouse is owned by the family that built it, and breaking a pane is a hanging crime. The day side is mirrors; the night side is the water.

w: temperate farmland world
s: green and brown patchwork with blue seas
lore: Small farms and big families, where the Collective's habit of raising children openly began as an ordinary local custom. The Hand calls it waste; the locals call it family.

w: grey-blue gas giant; free city-states drift on wide rafts across its wet cloud tops
s: grey-blue bands with pale drifting rain belts
m: two moons: a hazy giant and a smooth ice moon
r: rain-grown rice and algae, fuel gas, floating cities
lore: A rain-soaked giant whose cities are built on lifting rafts that drift wherever the wind takes them, growing rice in rain troughs on deck. Each city votes its own laws, and cities that disagree simply drift apart.

w: warm golden gas giant with a pale ring; a chain of festival barges, cable-bridged end to end, circles its equator
s: golden and cream bands, a red storm, a pale icy ring
m: one moon (cratered rock) and a broad pale ring
lore: A cheerful festival chain of barges strung end to end round the giant's equator, every barge with its own holiday each week. It is also where Locals from across the sector meet, hidden among the crowds that cross the cable bridges.

w: hot desert world, salt flats
s: ochre sand and bright white salt pans
lore: A desert world that sells chemicals and metals by the shipload and buys back every litre of water it drinks; its cities sit under shade roofs at the edge of the salt pans. The Water Guild sets the price of water, so the Water Guild runs the planet, and nobody has yet found a way to vote it out.

w: dry canyonland; water only in caves and on the canyon floors
s: tan rock cut by nine dark canyons
m: three small moons, all captured rock
lore: Thirty thousand people live in cave towns along nine canyons, each family hand-mining its own stretch of wall and drinking from the cave springs. They will not sell to Lode. Lode's surveyors keep having climbing accidents, and the canyon families keep sending polite condolences.

w: cold grey steppe, frozen most of the year
s: slate grey and pale green under frost, a grid of lit depots on the night side
pop: 2 billion hands, half of them in Tranche barracks
lore: The sector's Tranche depot, where new regiments muster in heated barrack grids and ship out. Above the parade ground hangs a debt board the size of a city block, showing every soldier's balance in lights. It goes down slowly, and some evenings the whole depot stands out in the frost to watch it.

w: warm ocean world, many islands
s: deep blue with green island chains
m: one small moon, pale cratered rock
lore: A warm sea scattered with islands whose councils meet once a year on a raft lashed together from every island's boats. Alma has twice offered to buy the coastline for an executive resort; both times the raft voted no, and the second vote was close.

w: gas giant; a free port floats at its breathable layer
s: sorrel-red and cream bands with two small storms
pop: 12 million traders and dockhands in the floating port
lore: A free port held up by hot-gas cells at the breathable layer, between Lode's refinery worlds, selling untaxed fuel skimmed from the clouds under its docks. The Hand tolerates it because half the executives in the sector refuel here off the books, and the port keeps very careful records of which half.

w: frigid mountain world, breathable
s: white peaks with dark blue valley shadows
lore: Herders live in turf-roofed valley towns under the frozen peaks, and their oldest law says no machine with a voice may be carried above the snow line. Praevisio wants a relay station on the peaks; its surveyors have to climb with paper maps and come back with frostbite.

w: hot volcanic world, refineries over glowing cracks, smog belts
s: yellow-grey haze lit orange by lava and refinery fires
m: one large moon, an industrial moon pitted with mine shafts
pop: 1.2 billion hands, Contract and Indentured, in sealed towns
lore: Lode refines crystal ore here in sealed towns over the lava cracks; the ore is cut from the moon above and dropped down in sealed pods. The pods land on a fixed schedule, and the towns under the drop zone are cleared eleven times a day. Residents are reminded that the schedule is published.

w: gas giant of turquoise and white bands; raft cities at the breathable layer
s: turquoise and white bands curling into spirals
m: two moons, one smooth ice and one dark ice-rock
r: music, art, fine textiles, fuel gas
lore: Its people live on raft cities of foam-glass lashed into archipelagos, which they sail through the clouds by trimming their lift and still call islands. Their songwriters supply half the music on Alma's broadcasts, under contracts nobody read. In lean years Alma buys the government too, and the songs get happier.

w: temperate plains and farmland
s: green and gold patchwork with blue inland seas
lore: A crowded free world of grain plains that has kept the Hand out for two centuries by paying every toll early, in full, every year. Its treasury is the most nervous office in the galaxy, and a single bad harvest would end its independence.

w: dry temperate world, flat basalt plateaus
s: pale tan and grey, circled by Lode's toll ring and its gate stations
pop: 900 million hands, most in customs and freight
lore: Lode's toll station on the Salt Lane: every ship pays at the gates of its orbital ring or is boarded. The inspection queue is so long that a market town has grown up on the waiting freighters, with its own schools, and some children have never seen the planet below.

w: cold tidally locked world; iron-red scrub along the twilight band
s: a brick-red twilight band under grey cloud, between a scorched face and a frozen one
lore: Continuity's labour prison for the sector, strung along the twilight. Inmates quarry the burnt day face in short shifts and are sent to the night face for discipline. Sentences are served by adding years to their Birth Debt, and parole is set by a Praevisio forecast. Nobody has been paroled early since; the Board considers this a success.

w: temperate world of mountains, valleys and forests
s: green valleys under white cloud
lore: Its valley mills spin the soft cream fabric of every gown in every Alma clinic. The weavers are not allowed to wear it, and each finished bolt is checked for hairs, which are traced back to the hand who shed them.

w: dry temperate world, desert and yard-city sprawl
s: dust-brown and grey under a hazy orbital ring of yards lit hazard yellow
m: one moon, quarried for hull steel
r: capital ships, hull steel, machine parts
pop: 5 billion hands, most of them yard crews
lore: Mordant's oldest yard world, where the family laid down its first hull. Every Mordant director is buried in the yard's foundations, and each new dock is poured over the last one's ashes. The yard crews say the docks are haunted, and they are not joking.

w: airless rock, hot days and freezing nights
s: pale yellow-white, cratered and scarred by gas pits, no cloud
pop: 20,000 hands, Indentured, in pressure huts on crawlers
lore: Twenty thousand hands boil rare gases out of the crust from pressure huts on crawlers, in a heat that kills drill crews faster than replacements arrive. Lode books the difference as attrition within tolerance, and the replacement ships now carry two crews.

w: hot humid gas giant; floating weed-mat villages in the warm cloud layer
s: deep green and teal bands dotted with bright storm spots
lore: Its villages are built on mats of gas-filled weed that grow in the warm cloud layer and ride the band winds round the planet. The mats split and rejoin every season, so the Hand's survey charts are always out of date, which suits the Runners who anchor among them.

w: cold tundra world, deep cave systems
s: white and grey-blue tundra pocked with dark cave mouths
pop: 300,000 hands, mostly vault technicians, living in the caves
lore: Praevisio keeps every forecast it has ever made in vaults under the tundra, the wrong ones included, and its technicians live down there with them. Nobody has ever been allowed to read the wrong ones. The Unruled have tried to burn it four times. The caves are too cold to burn.

w: cold world of mountains, highlands and ice caps; Alma is warming the highlands
s: white peaks over dark blue-green highlands
lore: Every soothing face and voice on Alma's news is cast here, in highland towns Alma is warming out from under the ice, a valley a decade. Children are graded for warmth of voice at six. The ones who fail are sent to the call centres.

w: cool world of glaciers, islands and marsh
s: grey-green marsh, white glacier tongues, dark sea
lore: Praevisio builds Gleaner drones here, and every drone is test-flown low over the marsh towns before delivery. The towns are told the passes are for calibration, and nobody has asked what is being calibrated.

w: pale gold gas giant; the wheat belts are on its living moon
s: pale gold bands, and beside them a moon striped gold and green
m: one living moon of wheat belts
pop: 200 million farmers on the grain moon
lore: A grain moon whose crop is bought before it is planted: Lode lends the seed and owns what comes up. In good years the farmers are free; in bad years the Hand owns the moon without sending a single soldier.

w: bright gas giant; the ranching plains are on its living moon, where the giant's glow and four more moons keep night away
s: bright cream and amber bands; a pale green moon among four others of different colours
m: five moons: the living ranch moon and four lamps, a white ice moon, a yellow sulphur moon, an orange hazy moon and a cream frozen moon
pop: 25 million ranchers on the living moon
lore: On its living moon the giant's glow and four coloured moons light the plains, so night never quite falls. The ranchers sleep in shifts and the town clocks have no hour marked night. Visitors go a little mad in the first month.

w: temperate world of plains, forests and cities
s: green and grey, studded with white relay domes
m: one moon covered in antenna fields
lore: Praevisio's listening world: every signal sent in the sector passes through its relays, and two billion hands work as readers, checking what the machine flags. They are told the job is temporary.

w: Mordant's refit ring: a built band round a star, with island seas on its floor
s: a steel loop round a white star; grey-blue seas and green island chains on the floor, piers on the outer hull crowded with damaged ships
m: none (a built ring round its star)
pop: 800 million hands, mostly dock crews, living on the ring floor and in the rim walls
lore: Mordant tows its damaged hulls here and berths them at piers along the outer hull. The crews call it the hospital, and Mordant bills each crew for the days their ship spends in dock, so most ships leave before the repairs are finished.

w: frigid world of mountains and fast rivers
s: white with dark river lines and blue glacier lakes
m: two moons: a dark ice-rock and a smooth white ice moon
lore: A frozen river world where Runners lay up their ships each winter in caves cut along the fast rivers. Its one town doubles in size when they arrive, and everyone pretends not to know what is in the holds.

w: rocky desert at the equator, forested highlands at both poles
s: a rust-red belt between two dark green caps
pop: 700 million, split between a northern and a southern state
lore: A burning desert belt splits the world in half. North and south have been at peace for a century only because neither can cross it. The Hand has offered each of them a bridge.

w: temperate grassland, hills and forests
s: soft green and brown under wide cloud bands
lore: Six billion farmers and townsfolk with no navy and a famous militia that drills every rest-day on the village greens. The Hand has counted the rifles and keeps its offers polite.

w: cold ice world
s: blinding white with blue crevasse lines
pop: 9,000 human ice cutters and about 4,000 Kiru exiles, in a station under the ice
lore: Ice cutters share an old mining station under the ice with a small community of Kiru exiles. The Kiru pay their rent in repairs, and the station has never run so well. Praevisio has flagged the whole planet.

w: dry tidally locked world with thin air; the junction town sits in the twilight
s: dark grey under a violet dusk haze: a burned day face, a black night face, and the town's lights along the twilight
m: one small moon used as a fuel depot
lore: Four unmarked Runner routes meet here, and the town lives in the violet twilight, with solar fields on the day face and fuel stores in the night. Lode has been suing the planet for sixty years over who owns the empty space between it and the next star; the case has outlived three judges.

w: temperate forest world of old groves and long rivers
s: deep green with silver rivers, thin cloud, few lights
lore: The first settlers swore that no tree older than the settlement would ever be cut, and two centuries later the oath still holds. Lode's timber buyers come every year, and the foresters walk them through the oldest groves until they leave.

w: warm, wet farm world of flat plains drained and seeded by Lode
s: neat squares of green and gold between straight canals and a shallow sea
lore: Lode drained these marsh plains and seeded them a century ago to feed the city-world next door. Fields are rented by the furrow to the families who work them, and the rent rises with the yield, so a good season is the most frightening thing that can happen.

w: barren rock mined down to its hot mantle, no water, no air worth breathing
s: dull rust-brown pocked with vast pits that glow orange at the bottom
pop: 4 million hands, Indentured, in sealed towns cut into the pit walls
lore: Lode has mined this rock for so long that its deepest pits reach the glowing mantle. The crews live in sealed towns cut into the pit walls. Those on the bottom shift get a heat bonus, credited against their debt in arrears.

w: cool, dry tidally locked world; steppe and parade grounds in the twilight band
s: a khaki twilight ring with grey barrack grids, between a scorched brown face and a white night side
m: two moons, one cratered all over as a gunnery range
lore: The Pacifiers who keep order on the sector's city-worlds are barracked here in the twilight, out of sight, and rotated so the cities never see the same faces twice. They drill on the scorched day side and store munitions in the frozen night. Off duty they may not visit the cities.

w: city-world, one continuous city with sealed underlevels
s: grey and gold by day, a solid web of light at night, an orbital toll ring round the equator
m: none; only the orbital toll ring
lore: The city-world where two of Lode's busiest lanes cross, and the orbital ring round its equator is one long toll gate. It pays more tolls in a day than most sectors pay in a year. Its lowest levels have not seen daylight since the Receivership, and down there rent is charged for air.

w: sprawling city-world round a few inland seas
s: grey-brown sprawl round dark inland seas, ships stacked in orbit
lore: A free city-world of two hundred billion that is buying its independence from the Hand in instalments. The last payment falls due in nine years, and nobody on the planet believes the Hand will accept it.

w: calm gas giant; Alma's clinic cities hang under heated gas balloons at the warm, breathable layer
s: soft cream and blue-green bands, pale and quiet, one blush-pink storm
r: births, medicine, Birth Debt contracts, some fuel gas
pop: 200 million hands in the balloon cities, mostly clinic staff and mothers under contract
lore: Alma's birth clinic for the sector hangs in the giant's cream clouds, its wards slung under heated gas balloons at the layer where the air is warm and breathable. It bills forty million births a year. Every newborn is issued a Hand number and a first statement before it is washed.

w: frigid world of frozen lakes, black forests and cold seas
s: dark green forest broken by white frozen lakes, ice at both ends
lore: Praevisio's forecast lab: a whole world of hands lives under total observation in heated towns between the frozen lakes, so the machine can test its forecasts on them. They are paid a small bonus to behave normally, and nobody is sure any more what normal was.

w: hot volcanic world, foundry belts along rivers of lava and slag
s: dark grey with glowing orange river lines, foundry lights across the night side
pop: 1 billion hands in ash-roofed foundry towns
lore: Mordant's fittings works: bunks, galleys, hatches and lockers for every hull, stamped out by the million in foundry towns roofed against the ash. Its rivers run orange with lava and slag, and the towns hold one holiday a year, on the day the presses are cleaned.

w: cold mountain world, glaciers in every valley
s: grey peaks, white glaciers, thin white cloud
lore: Its villages are built into cliff faces above the glaciers and reached only by cable car. One family owns every cable, so one family decides who visits, who leaves and who gets the doctor.

w: hot jungle world under constant rain
s: dense dark green under white rain clouds
pop: 90 million, a third of them contract workers
lore: The plantation houses import workers on ten-year contracts to tap the jungle for medical compounds. Most go home owing more than when they arrived. Alma buys the yield, and in some years it buys the government.

w: dry airless rocky world
s: dark grey and ochre, pitted with claim workings
pop: 400,000 claim miners, in pressure huts on their claims
lore: Independent miners work its rocks in family claims, each family in a pressure hut on its own pit. Lode buys their ore through middlemen at a third of the fair price, so lately the miners have been selling the best of it to the Collective instead.

w: hot humid swamp, mud flats and rainforest
s: murky green-brown under constant cloud
m: one moon, a single vast open pit
pop: 1 million swamp settlers and moon miners
lore: Its moon is one vast open pit, worked by a free crew that sells a rare heavy crystal. Twice the Hand has sent buyers. Twice the crew flooded the pit and waited in the swamp below until the buyers left.

w: dry barren world of gravel deserts, air too thin to breathe
s: pale grey-brown, no seas, no cloud
pop: 1.9 million miners in sealed well towns
lore: Water is mined from deep under the gravel and sold by the cup in sealed well towns. The well guild gives every child a share of the wells at birth: the one world in the sector where a newborn is owed something rather than owing it.

w: mountainous world with narrow seas
s: deep blue seas between brown mountain chains
lore: Two moons drag tides high enough to drown a city, so the coastal cities live behind enormous sea walls. The wall-builders' union decides where the next wall goes, which makes it the real government.

w: hot desert world with lava fields
s: tan desert, black lava fields, red glowing pits
pop: 2 million smelters and their families, in shielded towns
lore: Free smelter crews work ore in the natural heat of open lava pits, cheap and lethal, and sleep in shielded towns at the desert's edge. The Dust call it the Kitchen. Lode buys the metal and asks no questions about the crews.

w: cold slag-covered world, air too thin to breathe; green terraces under glass
s: charcoal grey with small green terraced patches
lore: Buried under slag dumped by a company that went bankrupt before the Receivership. Grower families live in terraces under glass and compost the slag back into soil one terrace at a time; they reckon on four hundred years, and have done thirty.

w: pale blue gas giant off every lane; its one living moon is temperate hills and orchards
s: a pale blue gas giant and a green, blossom-white moon with blue lakes
m: one living moon of orchards and lakes
r: fruit, cider, wood, from the moon
pop: 15 million orchard townsfolk on the moon
lore: A quiet orchard moon of a giant that pays no tolls because no lane goes there. The townsfolk keep it that way by refusing to build a port big enough for a Hand freighter.

w: cold world of frozen plains whose thin air, left by a failed terraform, pools in deep craters
s: patchy blue haze over white plains and brown crater floors, changing week to week
m: three moons: two cratered, one a small captured rock
lore: An old terraform gave it air too thin to hold, and three moons drag what is left round the globe so it pools in the deep craters. Every town sits under a crater rim, and the rims are fought over every dry season.

w: tropical jungle world over deep cave networks
s: bright green under blue-white cloud
m: two moons, one grey rock, one pale ice
lore: A jungle mould grown in the caves here becomes the healing gel used in every Hand clinic and hospital ship. The hands who tend it heal fast, so they are kept working through injuries no other world would allow.

w: warm ocean world of rainforest islands
s: deep green islands in turquoise sea
lore: Its island stills brew untaxed copies of Alma's healing gel. Alma's lawyers call it theft. The patients who can't afford the real thing call it the cheap jar, and some of them come back.

w: cool dry world under an upper air made crushing by a failed thickening; people live in crystal caves
s: opaque pale violet haze over dim tan ground
lore: A failed thickening left the upper air heavy enough to crush a ship, so everyone lives in crystal caves below, reached by one deep lift. Whoever holds the lift holds the world. It has changed hands nine times.

w: mild ocean world of island spires, raised and seeded green by Alma
s: blue sea studded with white spires and green hilltops
m: two moons, one pale cratered rock, one cream ice
lore: Alma raised the island spires from the seabed and seeded them green for Executive-grade villas and thousands of smiling staff. No executive may be told bad news while on the island, so bad news waits on the docks, sometimes for weeks.

w: tidally locked world; red mesas and green river valleys along the twilight band
s: a red-orange twilight belt threaded with green valleys, a scorched day face and a white night face
m: one moon, a pale cratered rock
lore: A trading world strung along the twilight band, where Hand money is refused and everything is bartered or paid in fuel. Mirror farms on the day side make the fuel, and the night side's glaciers feed the rivers. Lode's toll collectors leave with purses full of goods they can't account for.

w: amber gas giant with one great dark storm; refinery rafts ride the winds round its edge
s: amber and cream bands with one dark storm
m: eleven small moons (the five largest drawn)
lore: Free skimmer families live on refinery rafts that ride the winds round the edge of the great dark storm. They dive their ships into the cloud tops for fuel gas and sell it at half Lode's price, and Lode's freighters keep accidentally ramming their skimmers.

w: crowded world-city grown over forests and mountain spines
s: grey-green sprawl with dark mountain spines, lit end to end at night
m: two moons, one grey rock, one dark ice-rock
lore: A crowded forest world grown into one city, which sells itself to the Hand in bad decades and buys itself back in good ones. The paperwork is kept ready in both directions.

w: temperate river world, wet lowlands and rice terraces
s: green-brown lowlands laced with silver rivers, small blue seas
lore: Every year its river towns draw lots for a governor, who serves one year and may never stand again. Once the lot fell on a Hand informant. He resigned in a week, citing the workload.

w: searing volcanic world, radioactive lava seas and black glass plateaus; suits required outside the bunkers
s: black glass plateaus between glowing orange seas
pop: about 3,000 people in suits and shielded bunkers
lore: Radioactive lava seas and plateaus of black volcanic glass. A Continuity outpost and a Collective camp sit in shielded bunkers on opposite plateaus and have quietly agreed not to shoot each other, because the planet does it for them.

w: temperate city-world, archive towers over the old continents
s: grey and white, few open spaces, small dark seas
lore: A free city-world that keeps paper archives of every world's history from before the Receivership. Praevisio has offered forty times to digitise them for free. The archivists have the forty letters on file.

w: warm wet plains of tall grass and marsh, grey rock spires, slow rivers
s: gold-green marsh plains under haze, grey rock spires
lore: The marsh towns build small starships in barns on stilts, and every harvest fair ends with a race. The Walkouts send scouts to every fair, and the winning pilot rarely goes home.

w: cool gas giant; towns slung under gas balloons ride the breathable layer
s: blue-grey and pale green bands, one small grey moon
lore: Its balloon towns rent the orbit to whoever pays: some years a Hand customs post, some years a free market. The locals keep two flags in every gondola and fly whichever is cheaper that year.

w: azure gas giant; domed guild cities float on vacuum cells, moored to one another in a lattice
s: bright blue bands with white storms, thin dark rings
m: no moons; a set of thin dark rings
r: luxury goods, fabric, jewellery, fuel gas
pop: 850 million in the floating guild cities
lore: Its guild houses make jewellery and fine clothes for Hand executives in domed cities moored together above the blue, and are proud of never selling to anyone else. The Collective calls them the Board's tailors and has their order books.

w: dun gas giant with a dense dust-haze layer; open refit rafts drift on the haze
s: dun and pale green bands under ochre haze, a faint white ice ring fed by its one moon
m: one moon, an icy geyser moon that feeds a faint ring
r: ship refits, new registries, fuel gas
pop: 1 million painters and crews on the rafts
lore: A gas giant on the Trunk Line where crews repaint and rename ships on open rafts drifting in the ochre haze. Every hull that leaves has a new registry, and the painters swear they have never seen it before.

w: grey-tan gas giant; nobody lives in its clouds
s: tan and grey bands, crowded by thirteen mined moons
m: thirteen moons, all mined; the three biggest are plated over with works
r: alloys, ore, carved stone from the moons
lore: Thirteen moons crowd its sky, each claimed by a different mining family. Once a year the families meet on an old barge in the cloud tops to settle their disputes, and that is the only time anyone goes down.
