w: dry industrial world under heavy smog, no open water, foundry cities
s: brown-grey under yellow smog, a dark factory moon
m: one moon covered by an abandoned arms factory
lore: An old foundry world with no open water left, whose moon holds an arms factory abandoned when the Republic went bankrupt. It still holds stock, and every year three buyers bid for it and the foundry councils sell a little more.

w: cold, dry tidally locked world with thin air; one face always to the sun
s: a pale blue-white frozen face and a bronze scorched one, joined by a thin seam of glowing cooling vents along the twilight
pop: 60,000 hands, Staff grade technicians, in sealed archive halls
lore: Praevisio's sector archive: every purchase, message and heartbeat in the sector's holdings is copied here within the hour, into halls cut under the night face where the cold keeps the machines quiet. Their heat vents glow along the twilight. Staff are rotated every ninety days so nobody learns what the archive is for.

w: frozen high mountain world, cold winds, no open sea
s: dark granite grey with snow-white ridges, a few garrison lights in the passes
pop: 2 million hands, mostly Contract grade soldiers and families, in heated galleries under the peaks
lore: Continuity's mountain garrison, cut into the peaks above the Yard Road, its barracks and families buried in heated galleries under the snow. Its watch posts can see every toll beacon in the sector, and its gunners fire on any ship that skips a toll, with Lode paying a bonus per hit.

w: warm, humid ocean world, its seas drained basin by basin into salt flats
s: deep blue seas edged with blinding white salt pans
r: salt, sea metals, brine chemicals, farmed fish
lore: Lode drains the seas here a basin at a time and sells the salt and the metals left behind. Each dried basin is renamed with a catalogue number. The coastal towns move every decade, chasing the shoreline.

w: temperate world, rolling green valleys
s: green and soft brown under scattered cloud
pop: 40 million settlers in old family holdings
lore: Orchard families who have farmed the same valleys for three hundred years and pay Lode's toll in fruit rather than credit. The Hand has offered to buy the valleys twice; the third offer, everyone knows, will be a foreclosure.

w: warm jungle and mountain world, terraformed by Alma, with gentle engineered rains
s: rich green with mist-filled valleys
pop: 520 million hands, mostly Staff grade service workers
lore: Alma's rest world for executives, terraformed from bare red rock two centuries ago; even the rain is scheduled, warm and gentle, every afternoon. Terraced jungle retreats where nothing is billed and nothing is remembered. The staff are chosen for their beauty and their calm, and sign a contract never to leave the planet.

w: airless mountain world, its old domed cities in decay
s: ochre and grey cratered rock, the dull lights of old domes in the valleys
pop: 300 million hands, mostly Contract grade, in pressure domes and tunnel towns
lore: Alma brews the happiness pill here, in mountain factories above domed towns whose seals are failing one by one. The workers are paid in pills, so the towns are very calm and very poor. Local cells keep a dry house in the old tram tunnels under the domes.

w: temperate rainy world, oceans, plains and rivers
s: blue and green, streaked with brown river deltas
lore: A wet farm world where three great rivers meet the sea. The settlers sell grain to anyone, Hand or not, and every harvest season the Hand's buyers and the Runners' boats tie up at the same docks without looking at each other.

w: temperate gas giant; a breathable layer under the cloud tops, crowded with floating foundry cities
s: grey-brown and dull green bands, smudged with forge soot, one dark storm in the south
r: weapons, machine parts, manufactured goods, fuel gas
pop: 9.3 billion citizens of the free floating cities
lore: A free gas giant of nine billion that makes weapons for anyone who pays: Continuity, Repossessors, the Collective. Its foundry cities float on the heat of their own furnaces; a city that stops working sinks. The gunsmith guilds keep it free by keeping both sides armed. It works until one side wins.

w: temperate farm world, fields, forests and mountains
s: golden plains with dark green forest belts
lore: The breadbasket of the Trunk Line: endless wheat under a big sky. Its settlers remember the famine before the Receivership, which is why many of them quietly like the Hand's freighters.

w: volcanic rocky world of steam and thermal pools; domed towns over the pools
s: charcoal grey dotted with turquoise and orange pools
lore: A volcanic world of hot springs, where the settlers built domed towns over the thermal pools and heat every home for free. Hand executives come to bathe in secret, because there is nothing like it in Alma's resorts.

w: temperate forest world, cool and green
s: deep green with silver lakes
lore: Forest settlers who never cut a tree without planting two. They sell food down the Trunk Line and buy nothing they can't repair. Growers come here to learn, and the forest families quietly teach them.

w: cold airless rock; the free port lives in pressure halls under the highlands
s: slate blue with ice-grey highlands
lore: A free port on a cold, airless, moonless rock, where Runners refuel off the toll lanes in pressure halls cut under the highlands. Its harbourmaster keeps two sets of books, and the Hand has only ever seen one of them.

w: volcanic world, hot and ash-heavy, refinery cities on the vent fields
s: black rock veined with glowing orange rivers under brown ash
r: fuel isotopes, heavy metals, construction materials, smuggled goods
lore: A volcanic industrial world of nearly six billion that refines fuel isotopes and sells them on and off the books. Half its population works the vents, the other half works out which side to sell to this year.

w: cool wet moorland world
s: olive and brown under constant grey cloud
lore: Peat-cutting settlers on a damp, quiet moor world. Nothing much happens here, which is why the Collective's wounded are sent to recover in its farmhouses.

w: small gas giant; a ring of floating towns rides the rim of a storm that never dies
s: green-tan bands with long white cloud streaks and one great pale storm
lore: A ring of small towns rides the rim of a storm that has never died, circling it every few days. The mayors sign whatever the Hand puts in front of them and then ignore it. Organisers from the Hand worlds meet in the guest houses, and the mayors have never asked their names.

w: warm island world, greened by Alma from bare reef rock
s: turquoise sea dotted with bright green islands
pop: 8 million hands, mostly Staff grade media crews
lore: Alma greened these islands from bare reef rock to film its broadcasts: smiling hands on white beaches, sold to the galaxy as ordinary life. The actors are hands from the inner worlds who won a lottery. Few ask what happens to them when the season ends.

w: cool ocean world, one harbour city sprawling along its single long coast
s: dark northern seas, a grey urban sprawl along one long coast
lore: A grey harbour city on the Trunk Line that pays the Hand's taxes and keeps its own police. Continuity has offered to 'assist' with security three times. The city council has politely declined three times.

w: a built ring round its star: a cold mountain floor under snow, its casino towns terraced up both rim walls
s: a white and grey band round its star, the rim walls glittering with casino lights
m: none (a built ring round its star)
lore: Alma's pleasure ring, built round its star for executives who want snow on demand. Casino towns climb both rim walls, and six billion service hands staff the tables where executives bet their own employees' Birth Debts. A hand can wake up owing a different supervisor because of a card game.

w: gas giant; Lode's old refinery decks float on a dense lower layer of gas like ships on a sea
s: brown and amber bands with one slow orange storm
m: two moons, one scarred by old open pits
pop: 2 billion people on the floating refineries, many ex-refinery crews
lore: Walkouts seized Lode's refineries here, great decks that float on a heavy layer of gas like ships on a sea, and now run the Collective fleet's fuel from them. The decks still carry Lode's stencils, painted over by hand with the names of the crew who took them.

w: temperate world of salt flats and canyons where the seas were drained, salt marsh spreading back along the old shores
s: white salt plains edged with new green marsh
lore: Lode drained the seas here and left the planet as salt flats. The Growers are bringing it back one marsh at a time, planting salt grass in the brine of the old shorelines and living in sod huts at the edge of the green. Nobody lived here ten years ago. Now six thousand do.

w: airless rocky world, Lode's toll station in close orbit
s: deep red under the station's lights
m: no natural moons; the toll station, a hollowed rock plated in red steel, orbits close
pop: 500,000 hands, mostly Contract grade toll staff, on the station and in sealed depots below
lore: Lode's toll station on the Long Haul, a hollowed rock painted blood red so no captain can claim to have missed it. A skipped toll is paid in crew: one Indentured hand per unpaid jump, signed over to Lode on the spot.

w: small rocky asteroid world, low gravity, no air
s: black and grey, scarred with pit lights
pop: 30,000 Dust families in tunnels under the pits
lore: A Dust mining rock that the miners own outright since the night they welded Lode's overseers into their own office. The families live in the old tunnels, still mine, and now sell the ore to the Collective at no price at all.

w: gas giant where two lanes cross; the free market is a town of rafts lashed together at the breathable layer
s: blue-green and cream bands inside broad pale rings, its orbit thick with freighter traffic
m: one small moon, and broad pale rings
pop: 90 million traders and settlers on the market rafts
lore: The crossing of the Long Haul and the Salt Lane, and the busiest free market between them: thousands of rafts lashed together in the clouds, cast off and tied on again as traders come and go. Everyone trades here, and the Unruled have twice tried to blow up the Hand's customs office on the main dock.

w: dry plains world scarred by old mining, replanted in green strips around a prefab town
s: tan and green with grey prefab towns and old pit scars
lore: A town of a million built from Hand prefab that Lode abandoned, with green strips spreading over the old mine plains around it. The Locals run the replanting by committee, the Unruled refuse to attend, and they argue about it every evening in the same canteen.

w: temperate world, hills and farmland
s: green and ochre with dark hilltop forts
lore: A fortified hill town and its farms, built by settlers who survived three raids before the Receivership. They still close their gates every night, and they open them to anyone who knocks.

w: cold world of frozen hills; the lowland pastures are slowly being warmed
s: white uplands round green-grey lowland pastures, long cloud bands
lore: A cold world of shepherds and stone farms, far from the lane, where each family runs buried heat lines under its fields and thaws one more pasture every few years. Praevisio flags it every year as 'low data', which means nobody has told it anything worth knowing.

w: temperate world of rivers, lakes and meadows
s: green land laced with pink rivers and pink lakes
lore: Its rivers and lakes run pink with a harmless algae, and the dyers' guilds steep their cloth in them. Alma's design studios have offered to buy the dye recipes. The settlers suspect Alma already took them.

w: hot cratered world locked to its star: one face burnt, one frozen, a habitable twilight band between
s: burnt orange day side pocked with craters, a thin line of white lab domes along the twilight band, a blue-black night side
pop: 200,000 hands, Staff grade researchers, all under domes
lore: Praevisio's forecast lab sits in a string of white domes along the twilight line, models the next ten years of the frontier, and dumps its heat onto the frozen night side. The scientists here are the only hands who can read their own forecasts, and many of them choose not to.

w: hot desert world, dry, its dunes cut into sand pits
s: pale gold dunes under a hard blue sky, the pits showing as pale scars
m: two small moons, both captured rock
pop: 13,000 hands, mostly Indentured, in sealed pit barracks
lore: Lode sifts this desert for the pure sand that Praevisio melts into server glass. The quarry crews sleep in sealed barracks by the pits and breathe the sand anyway, and every server window carries a little of their lungs.

w: mild mountain and jungle world; Alma terraformed its frozen peaks into cool green valleys
s: deep green with white clinic terraces on the peaks
lore: Alma softened the frozen peaks above the jungle into cool valleys for its frontier birth clinic. Mothers are flown in from all over the sector and flown home alone. The newborns go into Alma's books with interest from the first breath.

w: temperate world landscaped over its vaults: coasts, canyons, forests and hills
s: blue and green, its cities bright along the beaches
r: debt registry, legal offices, food, tourism
pop: 800 million hands, mostly Staff grade clerks
lore: The Board landscaped a dead world into pleasant beaches to sit on its frontier registry: every Birth Debt in the sector is filed in vaults under the sand. Its clerks are the best-paid hands on the frontier and the worst-guarded, because the Board considers paper boring.

w: cold dry world of mesas and scrap fields
s: rust-brown under thin dust, glittering with scrap
pop: 1.5 million hands, mostly Indentured yard crews
lore: Mordant's breaking yard: old hulls are towed down to the cold mesas and torn apart for steel, and the crews sleep inside the hulls they strip. Mordant's lifers are signed to one hull for life, so when a hull is broken here, its crew is broken up with it and resold.

w: frigid mountain world, caves and hot springs
s: white snowfields cut by steaming dark valleys
lore: Continuity's labour world: frozen mountains, deep mines, and hot-spring valleys roofed in glass where the guards live. The prisoners sleep in the mine galleries. They are hands who fell too far behind on their debt, and they mine it off at a rate Continuity sets every year.

w: cold world of icy tundra and caverns
s: white and blue-grey, with a short brown summer at the equator
lore: Hunters and trappers live in heated caverns through a winter that lasts half the year, and come up onto the brown tundra for the short summer. The Hand lets them be, because no forecast has ever found a reason to want this world.

w: temperate world of grasslands, lakes and hills, regrown by the Growers
s: green and gold with large blue lakes
pop: 400,000 people, with a small Kiru exile community
lore: Lode stripped this world and left it for dead. The Growers let it lie fallow for forty years, seeding it a valley at a time, and now it is grassland and great lakes again. The Collective runs its biggest schools here, which the Hand calls the most dangerous thing it owns.

w: gas giant in constant storm
s: bruised purple and grey bands lit by lightning, inside a heavy dark debris ring
m: five moons, the smallest a broken stump inside a heavy debris ring
pop: 40,000 people on skimmer platforms and the moons
lore: A storm-wrapped gas giant whose skimming families pull fuel from the clouds and sell it to both sides, working from platforms anchored above the storm deck on kilometre-long drogue lines. Lode wants the gas. The families have mined the debris ring with old charges, and they say so.

w: cold world of cliffs, glaciers and ice caves
s: white and blue with dark cliff walls
pop: 8,000 hands, Staff grade technicians, living in the ice vault
lore: Praevisio's cold vault, cut into the glaciers so the ice cools its machines; its technicians live in the ice with them. It sits one jump from Fallow and listens to it. The Unwritten pray for the day the ice melts.

w: cold world of snow, ice and dry desert, slowly warmed by its greenhouse towns
s: white and tan, patched with shining greenhouse towns and spreading green
lore: Cold desert and ice fields where settlers grow sweet fruit under glass and dig clear gemstones out of the ice. Each generation the greenhouse towns spill heat and green a little further over the tan. Its people are known for reading faces; Repossessors avoid them.

w: lilac gas giant; vineyards and boatyards line the rivers of its one living moon
s: a lilac and cream gas giant beside a green moon threaded with silver rivers
m: one living moon of long rivers and vineyard slopes
r: wine, small boats, river trade, all from the moon
lore: A river moon of vineyards and boatyards under a lilac giant. Its people take in whoever arrives, and half its villages now hide someone the Hand is looking for.

w: tidally locked world, warm dry plateaus along the twilight under a sun that never moves
s: a red-brown plateau band glinting with solar fields, between a burnt day face and a white night face
pop: 12 million settlers in the twilight towns
lore: Its settlers live in the twilight in towns of rammed earth, glaze the edge of the day side with solar fields under a sun that never moves, and haul ice from the night side for water. They sell power cells to the Collective and to Lode, and refuse to discuss it.

w: hot humid world of low wet forest
s: dark green with brown river mouths
lore: A humid world of small farms that grows the peppers and herbs of Collective kitchens. Its farmers once sheltered a whole Walkout yard crew, and still feed their grandchildren for free.

w: warm swamp world, dug into flooded pits
s: dark olive with black flooded pits
lore: A swamp world Lode is slowly digging up for brown coal. Each new pit floods and becomes another black lake. The pumps run day and night, and so do the crews.

w: brassy gas giant; the mint towns hang under balloons in the breathable layer
s: bronze and copper bands, two moons beside it
m: two moons: a mined moon of open pits and a cratered rock
pop: 5 billion settlers in the balloon towns and on the mine moon
lore: A gas giant that mints the last hard coins in the galaxy from metal dug on its moon, worth what the metal is worth and owed by nobody. Each mint town hangs under its own balloon. The Hand hates money that isn't debt, and the vaults are on every Board agenda.

w: temperate world of green hills and white stone towns
s: green hills with white stone towns
pop: 20 million settlers, descendants of old navy crews
lore: Settled by Republic navy crews who refused the Receivership and flew here with their ships. Their great-grandchildren still drill on the parade ground. The old ships no longer fly, and Continuity knows it.

w: ocean world with no land at all
s: deep blue with a scatter of grey floating towns
lore: A Runner town of old hulls lashed together on an ocean that has no land. A small Nhal exile community lives at its edge, and nobody asks them to move.

w: cold world of frost plains, thin forests in the valleys
s: white and grey-green, small stone villages in the valleys
lore: The Unwritten broke every machine on this world more complex than a pump. Praevisio's scout probes that fall here are hung in the square as trophies. Visitors leave their devices in orbit, or lose them.

w: dark gas giant; Unruled camps drift on rafts in the upper cloud
s: dark grey-green bands, almost no lights
lore: The Unruled call it nothing, so the map calls it Nowhere. Their camps drift on rafts of salvaged gas cells and go wherever the wind does; nobody answers hails and nobody signs anything. Two debt registries were burned by people who trained here.

w: tidally locked world; sunken stepwell gardens spread from the twilight into the hot day side
s: pale ochre day side dotted with dark green wells, a white night side
lore: Settlers farm deep, cool gardens in stepwells sunk into the day side, and each year the wells creep further toward the sun. Their water is cut from the night-side ice and piped across the twilight. The rights to it are older than the Republic, and the Hand's lawyers have spent forty years trying to read them.

w: cool city world of refineries under smog
s: dark grey sprawl under brown smog
r: heavy metals, fuel, chemicals, manufactured goods
lore: A city world of ten billion that refines metal and fuel for the whole edge of the map. It is free on paper, but its founding families have borrowed heavily from Lode, and Lode is patient.

w: hot desert world of ravines and salt beds where the seas were
s: orange-tan with pale salt beds in the old sea basins
lore: A desert world whose old seas have dried into deep ravines and salt beds. Its people live in towns dug into the ravine walls, mine metal in the dry beds and ration water by the bucket, and they sell to the Collective for water instead of credit.

w: frozen world of snow and ice, its sky lit green by auroras
s: white under a green glow of auroras
lore: An ice world where the sky burns green most nights. A few hundred families mine ice from heated shafts under the lights and believe the lights are their dead, so nobody flies at night for fear of disturbing them.

w: dry world of deserts and grassland, forest only along the rivers
s: tan and ochre with green river valleys
lore: A dry world settled by a dozen peoples who never agreed on one language, crowded along its green rivers. Its parliament still translates every speech six times, which slows everything down and keeps the peace.

w: cold arid world of glaciers, tundra and dark forest, its towns abandoned
s: white and dark green, its cities unlit
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a dark ice-rock
pop: about 3,000 Praevisio survey staff in one sealed town
lore: A cold world whose millions left in a single season sixty years ago; their cities stand dark under the frost. Nobody knows why. Praevisio keeps one sealed survey town here and a forecast filed for this world, and the forecast is sealed too.

w: polluted world of eroded wastes and industrial cities
s: brown and grey under thick yellow smog
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a captured rock
lore: A filthy industrial world of twelve billion, and the biggest free market off Lode's lanes. Smoke hides the docks, which is how the Runners like it.

w: barren airless world honeycombed with old mines and caverns
s: dark grey, washed pale green by its glowing moon
m: two moons, one glowing faintly green from an old reactor failure
lore: A barren world lit at night by a moon that still glows from a reactor failure long ago. Nobody lives here for good; about two hundred salvagers camp in sealed caverns, dig the old mines and pretend not to count the days.

w: hot desert world of mountains and oases
s: sand gold with dark mountain spines
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a captured rock
lore: A desert world of oasis towns where caravans still carry water by beast and the towns sleep through the noon heat in cellars. They take in exiles if they work, and a small Ilmar family runs the best well on the planet.

w: tidally locked world; mesa towns and highland plains along the twilight band
s: tan and red twilight band with green highland patches, a scorched day side and a white night side
lore: The Repossessors' market, where debtors caught on the run are sold back to whoever holds their debt. Its mesa towns line the twilight band, so a debtor who runs has the burning day or the frozen night to run into. Free, rich and quietly hated.

w: temperate forest world of lakes
s: deep green with private lakes
lore: A forest world settled by the rare hands who vested, paid off their Birth Debt and left. They live well and say nothing, and the Hand uses their quiet lives in its adverts.

w: dry mountain and canyon world
s: red canyons cut into dark mountains
pop: 290,000 settlers living in the old barracks
lore: An old Continuity garrison cut into the canyon walls, closed when its contract lapsed. Settlers moved into the barracks and herd goats on the canyon floors. The Hand still lists it as a holding, and still bills it for the rent.

w: warm forest world, heavy rain
s: deep emerald under thick cloud
m: two moons: a pale cratered rock and a small captured rock
lore: Rain forest so thick the settlers live in the canopy, on rope walks a hundred metres up. They trade wood and medicine, and the Collective's runaways vanish into their trees.

w: cold world of frozen mountains and fog-laced plateaus
s: grey-white plateaus laced with fog and frost
pop: 9 million hands, mostly Contract grade quarry workers in heated pit towns
lore: Lode quarries a grey stone here that holds fog in its grain, prized in every executive lobby. The mountain clans who once owned the quarries now work them from heated pit towns, and still sing their old names for each one.

w: volcanic world whose cooled-rock islands drift in seas of lava
s: black island crusts in a web of glowing orange lava
pop: 6 million settlers in domed island towns
lore: Islands of cooled crust drift in seas of lava. Fishing families who once worked a real sea now live in domes on the oldest islands, beside a few Runner crews. A new island hardens every few years, and the first family to land on it owns it, until it sinks.

w: dull brown gas giant; one floating town of fuel tanks
s: dusty brown bands with a few grey patches
pop: 20,000 Runners and families in one floating town
lore: A dull world on purpose: a Runner haven that looks like nothing from orbit. Its one town floats on its own fuel tanks, more tanks than houses, and when a strange ship arrives it floods them and sinks below the cloud tops until the ship leaves.

w: rust-banded gas giant; the red-grass steppe is on its largest moon
s: rust and cream bands, and beside them a red-brown moon under white cloud
m: four moons: a red-grass living moon, a cratered rock, a dark ice-rock and a small captured rock
pop: 6 million herders on the steppe moon
lore: A red-grass steppe on the giant's largest moon, where herders follow their animals and never stay, under three more moons. They are almost impossible to tax, and Praevisio has given up forecasting where they will be.

w: cold, dry tidally locked world; heated glass farms spread through its twilight band
s: a grey-gold scorched face, a frosted night face, and between them a thin band of green glasshouse fields and small new lakes
pop: 300 million settlers in the twilight band
lore: Settlers farm the cold twilight under heated glass, warmed by mirrors on the day face, and mark every year of life with a tattoo on the hands. The glass reaches a little further into the dark each decade. Lode has surveyed the night face twice for ore; the settlers are waiting for the third survey.

w: pale gas giant on the Long Haul; the tappers work its small ice moonlet
s: pale blue-white bands, and beside them a dull white moonlet with a single dock light
pop: 1,200 ice tappers in huts cut into the moonlet
lore: A small moonlet of ice circling a giant on the Long Haul. Its tappers live in pressure huts cut into the ice and sell water to passing freighters at a fair price, and Lode, which sells water further down the lane, has filed to have the moonlet reclassified as a navigation hazard.

w: hot jungle world of braided rivers and shallow seas
s: deep green, braided with brown rivers and steaming cloud
r: salvaged steel, fighter hulls, river ore
lore: Walkouts weld fighter hulls under the canopy where Speculators cannot see. The rain eats bare steel within a week, so every ship leaves half-built and is finished in orbit by whoever is free.

w: dry clear-cut world of stumpfields, regrowing
s: pale stumpfields with spreading patches of young green forest
lore: Lode clear-cut every forest here for pit props and the soil dried out behind it. The Growers plant one sapling for every name in each debt registry the Collective burns; the new forest is already taller than a person.

w: violent gas giant of storm belts; skimmer crews live on a tether hung from a moonlet
s: deep indigo with white storm bands and a faint dark ring
m: eleven icy moonlets (the five largest drawn) and a faint dark ring
lore: Dust crews live in pressure cans strung down one long tether that hangs from an icy moonlet into the upper clouds, and skim fuel gas in patched scoop ships. Every scoop is christened with the name of a crewmate the storms took, and the list is painted down the main tether.

w: airless mountain world of sharp ridges, with docks cut into the rock
s: pale tan and white, with sharp grey ridges
m: two small moons: one captured rock, one cratered
lore: A shipwrights' guild repairs freighters in airless mountain docks, where nothing rusts, and lives in pressure halls behind the dock walls. Mordant has offered to buy the guild three times; the last offer came with a Subpoena parked overhead.

w: temperate world of forests, caves and mountains
s: green and slate blue under thin cloud
m: one large white moon of smooth ice
lore: Four billion people build ship drives in factories dug into the mountain caves. The engine-makers' council sells to anyone who pays, and quietly fits the Collective's best drives at cost.

w: frozen world of crystal ice fields
s: glittering white with blue fractures
m: two moons, one dark ice-rock, one smooth ice
lore: The ice holds a crystal that keeps time better than any clock. Dust crews live in heated tunnels under the fields and mine it for the navigation cores of every ship, Hand or Collective, and the Unwritten still argue whether a clock counts as a thinking machine.

w: frigid world of snowy hills and mountains
s: white with grey-brown hills
lore: The Collective's oldest dry house, an old ore barracks dug into the snow where recruits come off Alma's pill. It takes a month; the screaming carries across the hills at night, and nobody here complains about it.

w: a broken shell older than the Republic round a dim red star; most of its plates have fallen
s: a dull red star behind a broken lattice of grey plates, wrapped in a band of rubble
m: none (a broken shell round its star; its fallen plates make a band of rubble)
pop: a few thousand Runners and Dust at any time
lore: A shell round a dim red star, older than the Republic, built by nobody anyone knows; most of its plates have fallen into a grey band of rubble. Runners and Dust squat in the plates that still hold, by one rule: nobody powers guns inside the shell, enforced by everyone shooting whoever does.

w: warm dry world of sand seas and oasis basins, breathable air
s: sand-gold with dark green oasis spots
m: one moon, a grey cratered rock
lore: Three old families own every water well and sell it by the litre to anyone landing. They have refused the Hand, the Collective and each other for ninety years.

w: volcanic world of black lava fields and grey-green ash forests, breathable
s: black and grey-green, glowing cracks under grey ash plumes
pop: 5 million herb-gathering clans in stilt towns
lore: The bark of a tree that grows only in the ash between the lava fields goes into Alma's healing gel. Herb-gathering clans live in stilt towns above the ash flows and sell it, and the Growers keep asking them, politely, to stop.

w: ocean world, no land
s: bright turquoise with drifting green dots
lore: No land, only ocean. Grower raft towns lashed together grow kelp and fish; when Gleaners come, they cut the ropes and scatter across a thousand kilometres of sea.

w: dry world of mountains, mesas and plains; factory towns line the old river beds
s: tan and brown mesas under thin dust
m: fifteen moons, one large; the five biggest are one large cratered rock and four captured rocks
lore: A free industrial world whose founding compact, older than the Receivership, binds it to sell to every side. Board lawyers have spent eighty years trying to void it; both sides meet here to trade prisoners.

w: dry rocky world, mesas and desert plains
s: rust red with ochre plains
lore: The towns are carved inside the red buttes to escape the heat. The dead are walled up in the rock behind the kitchens, so every family lives with its grandparents.

w: gas giant; the hardwood forests grow on its big living moon
s: brown and cream bands; its big moon green with snowy peaks
m: three moons: a big living moon of forests and mountains, a dark ice-rock and a captured rock
r: hardwood, rare minerals (both from the living moon)
pop: 30 million settlers on the living moon
lore: Loggers on its forest moon cut the hardwood that panels every executive cabin in the Hand's fleet. Under the roots lie rare minerals, and the families know the day they sell the forest is the day it ends.

w: cold mountain world, clear air
s: grey-white peaks over blue valleys
lore: A mountain post office, dug deep into the rock against the cold, keeps the galaxy's largest private letter archive. People pay to have letters held unread for decades, and the clerks have never once opened one, not even for the Hand.

w: gas giant
s: pale gold with amber bands
m: four moons: two dark ice-rock, one hazy giant and one captured rock
pop: 200,000 skimmer families in towns slung under helium balloons
lore: Independent skimmer families live in towns slung under their own helium balloons and draw fuel from the golden clouds. Lode's toll inspector visits monthly; the crews sell half their fuel to Runners before he arrives.

w: temperate world of plains, rainforests and oceans
s: green and blue with brown terraces
lore: Coffee co-ops grow beans on terraced plains above the rainforest. Sacks of Cafetal beans are the one currency every Runner port in the sector accepts without argument.

w: warm world of jungles, rivers, swamps and seas
s: brown-green delta fanning into blue sea
lore: A great river delta where a stilt-town market trades anything to anyone. Whoever owns the dredges that keep the channels open runs the market, and the dredges change hands about once a decade.

w: hot gas giant; its one living moon is grassland, jungle and mountains
s: a yellow-green and olive banded giant beside a small green moon
m: one living moon of grass, jungle and mountain spines
lore: The Table met on this giant's grass moon in secret for a year before the base moved on. The two thousand settlers still sweep the empty hall every week, in case it comes back.

w: barren airless rock
s: dark grey with a glitter of wreck fields
pop: 300 scrap dealers, living in the best of the wrecks
lore: A bare rock with one business: a scrap family that buys wrecks from both sides, lives in the best of them and asks nothing. It also sells wrecks back to their former owners, at a premium, with the bodies removed.

w: ocean world, shallow seas
s: pale aqua with sandbars
lore: Fishing villages here keep a second fleet of boats nobody fishes from. They ferry Runner cargo out past the reef to ships waiting in deep water, and the Hand's inspectors only ever find fish.

w: cold rocky world, no air
s: brown and black
lore: A Runner fuel dump dug into a cold rock halfway between nowhere and nowhere. The rule is old: whoever leaves last refills the tanks, and whoever doesn't is never fuelled again.

w: warm tidally locked world; grassy plains, deserts and mountains along the twilight band
s: a green-gold and tan band between a scorched face and a white one
lore: Ranching families herd cattle along the twilight, grazing the green-gold edge watered by the night side's melt and the tan desert toward the burnt face. Lode offered to buy whole herds as feed stock; half the families sold, and the other half have been feuding with them ever since.

w: temperate gas giant; one town hangs under a clear balloon in the rain layer
s: sky-blue and white bands with soft rain cloud
r: fruit, herbs and medicine grown under the balloon, fuel gas
pop: 1 million settlers in the balloon town
lore: Founded a century ago by Alma clinic staff who walked out together and built a town under a clear balloon in the rain layer of a giant, where it rains every afternoon. Their grandchildren still smile too much, and nobody here will talk about why their grandparents left.

w: cold rocky world; its farmers are warming their fields against the frost
s: grey stone and white frost with spreading green field patches
lore: A cold, stony farming world whose farmers warm their fields with buried heat pipes and wind-walls, winning a few metres of green from the frost each year. Its militia fought off a Continuity acquisition once with hunting rifles and a blizzard, and the farmers vote every spring on whether to join the Collective.

w: airless rocky world of sheer cliffs
s: bands of red and black rock
pop: 500,000 cliff diggers, in sealed galleries in the rock face
lore: Diggers cut ore from sheer cliffs, living in sealed galleries in the rock face, and lower it on cables to the haulers waiting below. Lode buys every tonne at a price it sets, because there is no other buyer within six jumps.

w: airless rock with one old court dome
s: blue-grey cratered rock with one lit dome
pop: 60,000 clerks and pensioners under the dome
lore: The last court of the old Republic still sits here, under a cracked dome on a dead rock. Its judges are all past ninety and hear the cases nobody files; the Board has never quite dared to close it.

w: slate-grey gas giant; a cloud colony lives in the calm eye of a great storm
s: slate-grey bands around one great pale storm
pop: 5 million settlers in the storm-eye colony
lore: The colony rides in the calm eye of a storm that has turned for three centuries. It drew lots and voted to host a Collective school for children stolen back from Hand clinics; six hundred study here, and the Hand calls it a retrieval waiting to happen.

w: hot gas giant of eight moons; the fever-root plantations are on its living moon
s: dark green and yellow-hazed bands, and a steaming green moon beside them
m: eight small moons, one a hot living moon of jungle and swamp
pop: 425 million planters on the jungle moon
lore: Planters on the giant's jungle moon grow a fever-root that Alma refines into medicine. Alma buys the whole crop at a fixed price, paid in credit at Alma stores; most planters now owe more than the land is worth.

w: hot, airless mountain world with salt flats
s: white salt flats between dark mountains
lore: Ships from every side come here to die. Hulls are beached on the hot salt flats and cut up by breakers in cooled suits, and the metal is sold back to whoever is winning that year.

w: storm giant of purple-grey cloud; settlers farm its lightning from floating towns
s: purple-grey bands lit by constant flashes
m: two moons: a dark ice-rock and a hazy moon
pop: 30 million settlers in towns slung under balloons
lore: Lightning strikes here several times a minute. Settlers live in towns slung under balloons and farm it into batteries with rods hung kilometres below; Lode wants the batteries, and Praevisio wants the storms to cool its servers.

w: volcanic world of sulphur geyser fields over a thin crust
s: mustard yellow and grey with orange vent glow
pop: 800,000 miners in a ring of sealed towns
lore: Sulphur miners live in a ring of sealed towns around the great geyser field. The geysers blow on a schedule the towns set their clocks by; nobody trusts any other time, and a late geyser empties the streets.

w: frigid tundra world, slowly greened under ice greenhouses
s: white with grey ice shelves and a scatter of green greenhouse fields
lore: Growers built ice greenhouses lit by stolen reactors, and each winter the green under the glass reaches a little further across the tundra. They feed three Dust belts, and the Dust feed them fuel; it is the one place the two strands work together without being asked.

w: warm world of jungles and oceans
s: green continents in deep blue sea
lore: The biggest Collective population in the sector, and the worst neighbours. The Unruled hold the south, the Locals the north, and they built a wall across the isthmus to keep the peace.

w: frigid mountain world
s: white peaks over grey valleys
pop: 3 million refugees in camps dug into the snow
lore: Hands who fled a harvest notice wait in mountain camps dug into the snow, for travel permits that never come. The camp is free, cold and full; the Collective recruits there weekly.

w: temperate garden world
s: bright green and flower-bright
lore: An old botanist family keeps the galaxy's largest seed vault. Growers want it to replant dead worlds; Lode wants it for its farm holdings. The family sells to neither.

w: dry world where a planted rainforest dies back and burns every year
s: green, gold and brown bands
lore: A Republic-era company planted a rainforest on this dry world and the rain never followed: every year the forest dries into savannah and the grass burns. Settlers move with the fire line, and children learn to read the smoke before they can read words.

w: barren rock, almost no air
s: dull brown
lore: A barren rock the Board once sold, twenty times over, to twenty buyers. Claimants' pressure camps still dot the surface, each with its own deed and its own guns.

w: rainforest world, wet and warm
s: dark green under heavy cloud
lore: Loggers and a Grower commune share the rainforest under a truce drawn on a map nobody agrees on. Both sides keep surveyors, and the surveyors drink together.

w: arid world, deep aquifers
s: tan and ochre, cloudless
lore: Twelve billion people live in towns built around wells drilled kilometres down. Lode's new wells go deeper, and the town wells are going dry one by one.

w: gas giant; the nomad steppe is on its big living moon
s: red-brown and gold bands; a green-gold moon
m: two moons: a big living moon of grass plains and dark hills, and a cratered rock
r: food, textiles, knives (from the living moon)
pop: 25 million nomads on the living moon
lore: Nomad clans herd across the grass plains of its big moon and meet once a year in council under the giant. Their vote swings the whole sector, so the Hand and the Collective send envoys every season.

w: temperate river world
s: green valleys and blue rivers
lore: Water mills grind grain from the plains worlds. The millers have kept the same price for a century and refused every buyer; the joke is they are the last honest business in the galaxy.

w: cold world of blue sand, forests and snow
s: blue deserts and white plains
lore: Fewer than ten thousand people, most of them run from Hand debt, living in sod-walled huts dug half into the ground. They grind the blue sand into glass and sell it to anyone who doesn't ask where they came from.

w: gas giant; one hospital city floats at the breathable layer
s: pale green and white bands
pop: 2 million people in one floating hospital city
lore: An old order of nurses runs the only hospital in the sector that bills nobody, inside an old liner hull that sinks a little every year and is pumped back up by its patients. Alma has sued them for sixty years, and they still take every patient.

w: temperate world of steep mountains and dark forest, cut by one deep gorge
s: dark green with grey ridges and small grey-blue seas
lore: Walkouts build fighters in workshops cut into the mountains and fly them out through one narrow gorge. Every pilot learns the gorge first; the ones who don't are buried at its mouth.

w: warm ocean world of reefs, lagoons and low islands
s: deep blue with turquoise lagoons and white reef lines
pop: 30 million harbour folk; several thousand Ilmar, Kiru and Nhal exiles aboard the arks
lore: The arks of the Harvested ride at anchor in the lagoons while harbour folk and Walkout crews refit them as warships. The exiles live aboard and seldom come ashore; the harbour people know better than to invite them.

w: arid world of fossil reefs and caverns on a dead seabed
s: white coral ridges on yellow sand
lore: An ancient seabed, its reefs turned to stone and its sea long gone. Four hundred Runners live in sealed coral caves out of the sand wind, and their listening post hears every ship that drops out of hyperspace nearby.

w: hot world of red canyons, spires and desert
s: red canyons under a wide glittering ring
m: a wide ring of hundreds of moonlets; the five biggest are captured rocks circling just outside it
lore: A crowded ring of moonlets wrecks careless ships. The descendants of crashed crews live in the shade of the canyon walls, salvage the wrecks and pilot newcomers through the ring, for a fee set by mood.

w: temperate world of forests, high plateaus and seas
s: green and blue with high pale plateaus
lore: The Unwritten hold this world, and no thinking machine may land. Walkouts deliver supplies by hand-flown shuttle; one carried a navigation computer once, and it was smashed on the pad.

w: warm ocean world of low islands and white beaches
s: sapphire seas and white sand islands
lore: White beaches and warm seas. Alma wants it as a rest world for executives; the fishing towns have refused to sell for twenty years, and Alma is a patient buyer.

w: volcanic world: glowing rifts split plates of scorched forest
s: dark green-black plates split by glowing orange rifts
lore: The crust here cracks open every few years and swallows a town. Each quake also exposes fresh ore, so the settlers build on stilts and skids among the last forests, mine the new cracks, and drag what is left of the town somewhere else.

w: warm dusty farming world of orange plains, half greened
s: orange plains with spreading green farm belts under thin cloud
lore: Grower communes are greening the orange dust one irrigated belt at a time, and the farms already feed The Moorings. The Hand embargoes the system every few months; the farmers wait it out, keep the grain dry and plant another belt.

w: gas giant of grey-gold cloud bands; the trading houses float at the breathable layer
s: grey-gold bands with one pale amber storm
pop: 5 billion citizens in the floating cities
lore: Billions live in a free city of trading houses: a thousand buoyant hulls chained together by bridges at the breathable layer. Its bankers lend to Hand holdings and Runner crews alike, and say they are only hedging.

w: temperate forest world
s: dark green
lore: Grower rangers have trapped every trail in the forest. Pacifiers no longer patrol it; Continuity sends Proxies instead, and the rangers count those too.

w: tidally locked world: a scorched desert face, a frozen night face, and a twilight band of sea and dark mountain chains
s: tan day side and white night side, a ring of blue twilight sea between them crossed by dark mountains
lore: Mordant's drafting offices design every hull in the fleet here, in long halls above the twilight sea. Mirror fields on the day side power the halls, the night side keeps the archives cold, and design flaws are traced to the desk that drew them.

w: hot storm world, scoured plains
s: grey-brown with swirling dust storms
lore: Every Tranche bound for the front musters on these storm plains. The wind is so loud orders are given by hand signal, and the depot keeps the books of every kill credited.

w: tidally locked world: forest and savannah in the twilight band between a burnt day side and a frozen night side
s: a ring of green and gold between a rust-red day side and a white night side
lore: A free world that decides each year by a public coin toss which side it trades with. Its towns crowd the twilight band, mine salt on the burnt day side and cut ice on the night side. Praevisio has never forecast the toss correctly.

w: tropical world, cleared rainforest
s: green with white factory grids
lore: Praevisio cleared the rainforest for its sensor works: every Speculator probe in the Hand is assembled here. The workers are tagged like the probes, and the factory knows where each of them sleeps.

w: temperate forest world of lodges and warm lakes, landscaped by Alma
s: soft green and pale blue
lore: Alma landscaped this world for its executives, all quiet forest lodges and warm lakes. A smile that slips three times in a season sends its owner back to the clinic for retraining, and nobody describes the retraining.

w: temperate world of plains, forests and depot towns
s: green and gold with grey depot towns along the freight roads
lore: Once Lode's farm-and-freight hub. The Locals took the depots in one night and now feed four Collective worlds, while Continuity masses two jumps away.

w: temperate world of fields, hills and lakes, brought back by Growers on land Lode stripped
s: golden fields and blue lakes
lore: Lode stripped this world and left; the Growers brought back its fields and lakes over two generations. They refuse every machine and bring in the grain by hand. Each autumn Unwritten pilgrims arrive by the thousand to help, and the Dust call the bread holy and buy it anyway.

w: tidally locked world; savannah and windy uplands in the twilight band between a burnt day side and a frozen night side
s: brown-gold savannah ring between a scorched face and a white night face
lore: The wind from the burnt day side to the frozen night side never stops. Herding clans graze the twilight band, keep their meat in night-side ice caves and sell power from salvaged turbines by cable to anyone who docks. Lode has offered to take over 'maintenance', and the clans know what that means.

w: temperate world of valleys and grey hills
s: green and grey
pop: 200,000 settlers and a few hundred Kiru
lore: A few hundred Kiru exiles farm the valley beside human settlers. They share the harvest and the well, never a table. Neither side is comfortable, and neither has left in thirty years.

w: rust-banded gas giant; an old prison barge moored in its cloud tops
s: rust-red and dark brown bands, four moons, one of them red
m: four moons, one of them the red ore moon
lore: Continuity closed the prison barge moored in its cloud tops as 'below target' and took the guards home, but not the prisoners. Six hundred of them still sleep aboard, fly out to the red moon each shift to mine its ore, and sell it to the Runners at their own price.

w: airless brown rock; the toll station and its pressure halls sit in a crater
s: brown and cratered
lore: A Lode toll station so thoroughly bribed that the bribes now appear in its books as a fee. Runners pass at a fixed rate, and the station has beaten its revenue target eleven years running.

w: warm, wet gas giant; buoy towers float upright with their keels hanging into the wet layer, where vines grow
s: green-grey and cream bands, a broad pale ring, four moons
m: four moons and a broad pale ring
pop: 1 billion left in the upper towers, down from six
lore: A city of floating towers half emptied by a market crash two generations ago. The tower tops are still lit; the lower decks, down in the warm wet layer, are choked with vines and run by brewers whose dark ale sells across the sector.

w: hot jungle world
s: red soil and green jungle
lore: Lode's plantation holding: red soil, hot jungle, and one crop every hundred days, shipped ahead of schedule. Workers who miss quota are reassigned to clearing new jungle, which is why the plantation keeps growing.

w: frigid world of dark forests, mountains and frozen passes
s: white and dark green
lore: Trapper clans guide anyone across the frozen passes for pay, no questions asked. That includes Repossessors, which is why runaways here hire two guides and trust neither.

w: arid dusty world
s: dusty tan, a grey factory sprawl
lore: Walkouts and Unwritten seized a Praevisio robot factory together. The Walkouts want to restart the line and build for the Collective; the Unwritten want it smashed. The line has stood still for two years while they argue.

w: temperate clinic world, one city from coast to coast
s: cream-white cities
lore: Alma's oldest clinic holding: thirty billion hands, most of them born here and billed before their first breath. Births are scheduled by quarter, and a late birth carries a surcharge.

w: sea-green gas giant; the herbalists' rain forest grows on its living moon
s: a pale sea-green giant, and beside it a jungle moon with drifting white rain bands
m: six moons: the living jungle moon and five small grey rocks
r: medicinal plants, foodstuffs, dyes, rare botanicals
pop: 70 million settlers' descendants on the living moon
lore: Its herbalists' guild grows half the cures sold in the sector in the rain-forest canopy of the giant's living moon. Alma offered to license the whole canopy; the guild burned its own seed vault the night before the vote, so there was nothing left to sign away.

w: cold rocky world whose made air is thinning away; one deep valley still holds enough
s: pale blue-grey under a thin haze, one dark valley
lore: An old atmosphere job, failing: the air leaks away to space a little every year. The settlers bought the planet from Lode at a discount, winched their one town under pressure domes into the deepest valley where the air is thickest, and are betting their grandchildren will still have something to breathe.

w: temperate world of forested mountains and valleys, planted in rows by an old colonial company
s: dark green ridges in long parallel stripes
lore: Its forests were planted in straight rows by a colonial company that went bust three centuries ago. Every family knows which rows were their great-grandparents' work, and they sell Lode only the timber their own family planted.

w: dry world of nitrate plains, copper mountains and white salt-lake beds
s: tan and ochre plains, white salt lakes, mine scars
lore: Saltpetre and copper pour out of its dry plains on the Long Haul. Lode charges the toll to leave and sets the price to buy, and the miners' cooperative calls that holding both ends of the rope.

w: dry plains world, long summers, irrigated grain
s: gold and pale green squares and circles to the horizon
m: one small white moon of ice
lore: A flat grain world that has never sold to Lode. Every autumn the farmers burn one full field unharvested, in sight of Lode's buyers, so the buyers know the price of a no.

w: temperate ocean world with crowded coasts
s: blue sea laced with bright coastal cities
lore: The largest free world in the sector, governed by eleven harbour cities that argue for months over everything. Alma pays its broadcasters to run its shows for free, and a third of the young already talk like the adverts.

w: gas giant, storm bands of hydrogen and ammonia; the family lives on a tethered skimmer platform
s: honey amber with brown bands and a faint dust ring
m: eleven small moons, the largest of them icy, and a faint dust ring fed by the innermost
pop: 3,000 skimmer crew on the tethered platform
lore: An amber-banded giant whose clouds the Brandt family has skimmed for nine generations, living on a platform that lowers its scoops into the cloud tops on cables. Lode has offered to buy them out every year for forty years, and every year the offer is lower.

w: dun gas giant; the herding clans live on its living moon of grassy uplands and deep valleys
s: a dun-brown banded giant, and beside it a green-brown moon under fast white cloud
m: two moons: the living highland moon and a small grey rock
pop: 9 million herders on the living moon
lore: Highland herders on the giant's green moon keep the Republic's old land titles framed above every hearth: the last legal papers the Hand never got round to voiding. Continuity posted a garrison here once and withdrew it as a poor use of contract hours.

w: temperate world of fields and managed forest, built up by Lode with ground rock from its mines
s: patchwork of green and pale yellow
lore: Lode built this farm holding on bare rock, spreading ground tailings from its mines until the land would grow. Every field has a Hand number like a hand does; when a field underperforms it is retired, and the crew who worked it is reassigned with it.

w: temperate ocean world of scattered islands
s: deep blue scattered with green and white islands, a thin dust ring
m: three moons, and a thin ring of dust shed by the innermost
lore: A world of small islands that vote one island at a time. Three island councils sold their islands to Alma for a resort and a clinic, and the other islanders no longer sail within sight of them.

w: gas giant; the settlers' towns hang under great balloons in the cold, windy high cloud layer
s: pale violet and grey bands over a deep green haze, a faint dust ring
m: three small moons and a faint dust ring
r: wind power, fuel gas, hanging-garden barley
pop: 8 million settlers in the balloon towns
lore: Its settlers live high in the cold, windy cloud layer, in towns hung under balloons, and never go down: the warm green layer below is where the first colony choked. They keep that colony's dead in a gondola hung from the edge of the oldest town, facing the drop.

w: cold mountain world, thin dry air
s: grey and white peaks, dark valleys
r: quarry stone, slate, ore Lode has not yet found
lore: Lode's surveyors come every ten years and always report the mountains 'not yet viable'. The villagers have bribed every survey team for a century, and the price goes up each time.

w: temperate dry world, sprawling cities on plains
s: tan plains crusted with city lights
lore: Forty family shipwrights still build fast freighters by hand here, in slips too small for warships. Mordant buys every yard that goes bankrupt and closes it, and the forty that remain build mostly for Runners.

w: subarctic world of tundra, swamps and decaying cities
s: grey-white with dark city scars
lore: A city that outgrew itself before the Receivership; half its towers stand empty and frozen, and the people huddle into the warm half. Its workshops make the cheap toys and kettles Alma sells as its own, with the labels sewn on after the toll.

w: small airless rock, hollowed out, a docking ring round its equator
s: dark grey, pitted, lit by a ring of docking lights
lore: A hollow rock where five unpaid paths meet, with a fuel depot bolted to it. There is no government, just a list of rules nailed to the docking ring and one woman who enforces them.

w: gas giant with a toxic cloud deck; the pump towns ride one band's current round the planet
s: murky olive bands under a yellow haze
pop: 6 million in the drifting pump towns
lore: The air here will kill you in a day. The pump towns ride the current of one band, circling the planet every forty days; everyone wears a mask from birth, a bare face on deck means a visitor or a corpse, and Lode buys the methane they pump.

w: humid subtropical swamp and jungle world
s: dark green, steaming, cloud-wrapped
pop: 4 million hands, most of them Tranche recruits
lore: Continuity's jungle training ground, where new Tranches learn to fight in heat and rot. The recruits who fail are kept on as terrain staff, playing defaulters in the exercises until the exercises wear them out.

w: desert world where a failed atmosphere job turned the rain to acid
s: sickly yellow-white clouds over pale sand and dead grey lake beds
lore: A Republic firm seeded this sky to make rain, and the rain came down acid. Nothing lives outside the domes. Every building is coated in wax renewed monthly; the oldest house has four thousand coats, and the chemists distil the rain and sell acid to every refinery in reach.

w: temperate world of oceans and coastal forest
s: blue oceans, green coasts, one scarred grey moon
m: one moon covered in old wrecks
lore: Its single moon is still strewn with wrecks from the Republic's last war. The coastal towns live by salvaging them one bolt at a time, and sell the metal to anyone who lands.

w: pale gas giant
s: pale orange with soft cream bands
m: twenty-six moons, a dozen with hidden camps; the five biggest are a hazy giant, two dark ice-rocks, a smooth ice moon and a captured rock
r: hidden camps, fuel gas, moon-ice water
pop: 30,000 Runners and Dust families in camps on the moons
lore: A pale gas giant with twenty-six moons, and Collective camps dug into the ice of a dozen of them. Every forty days the camps move to another moon by lot, so the Hand's survey probes never find the same camp twice.

w: temperate world of canyons, caverns and forested valleys
s: green valleys cut by deep red canyons
r: cast hull frames, steel, ship parts
pop: 500 million hands, mostly Indentured yard families
lore: Mordant's outer-rim foundry, casting hull plate in the canyons for the yards further in. The canyon walls carry the stencilled number of every hull it has plated, and under each one the numbers of the crew who died on it.

w: warm living world of plains, forests and tidy jungle gardens, landscaped by Alma
s: green and gold with white resort coasts
m: three pale moons: two smooth ice moons and a frozen-plains moon
lore: Alma landscaped this jungle into tidy gardens over sixty years, as a rest world for Mordant and Continuity executives under three pale moons. Guests may buy a server's Birth Debt over dinner as a tip, so the staff compete for tables.

w: temperate gas giant; one great floating market city rides its breathable layer
s: grey-brown and sage-green bands
r: trade goods, finance, warehousing, fuel gas
pop: 2 billion free citizens in the floating city
lore: A free market city of two billion, ten thousand lift-hulls lashed into one mesh at the breathable layer, undercutting Hand prices across the sector. Its merchants' guild has one law above all others: no loan may run longer than a year, and no debt may pass to a child.

w: cold, dry tidally locked world; server halls dug into the frozen night face, cooling lakes at twilight
s: a pale grey day face, blue-white cooling lakes along the twilight line, and a black frozen night
pop: 6 million hands, mostly Staff grade, in the twilight
lore: Praevisio's forecasting node for the sector: server halls dug into the frozen night face, their heat bled into cooling lakes along the twilight, where the staff live. The day face is left to bake. Each morning the staff receive their own forecast; nobody has been shown the forecast for the holding itself.

w: airless rocky world of tungsten pits
s: dull brown with grey pit scars
pop: 20 million hands, mostly Indentured miners in pressurised pit towns
lore: A tungsten mine the size of a continent, worked from pressurised pit towns on a bare rock. Dust-lung is so common that Lode's clinic bills it as a pre-existing condition, back-dated to birth.

w: hot world of lava vents and rocky scrub
s: black and rust with glowing orange seams
lore: Settlers cook, heat and power their towns from volcanic vents, and build every town on skids. The vents move, so every town keeps a vent-reader who says when to pack up, and the vent-readers are right about two times in three.

w: cold highland world of lakes and plateaus, its valleys being warmed
s: blue lakes scattered over grey-green highland and snow
pop: 5 million settlers and a few thousand Kiru exiles
lore: Settlers warm the valleys one at a time with buried heat lines, and each thawed lake gets a town. Sixty years ago they gave one valley to a Kiru ark crew; the Kiru still pay rent every year in fish they don't eat, so that they owe humans nothing.

w: grey-green gas giant; workshop towns float on hollow hulls, chained into strings by cable bridges
s: grey and olive bands with one small pale storm
m: one small moon, a grey cratered rock
r: boot kits, synthetic leather, cheap goods
pop: 60 million workshop families in floating towns
lore: Workshop towns ride on hollow float-hulls, chained together by cable bridges so a whole string drifts as one. They make cheap boots in flat-pack kits; a broker sells them to Continuity's quartermasters, so half the Tranches march in boots made by people who hate them.

w: temperate marsh world of brown lakes under low light
s: brown and green with dark lakes
m: two small moons: one grey rock, one captured rock
lore: Its brown lakes are full of a fish that bites only at dusk, so the whole world works by night and sleeps through the day. Hand inspectors arrive in the morning and find everyone asleep.

w: temperate world with two large continents
s: two green-brown continents in a blue sea, the northern one scarred by mines
r: ore in the north, grain in the south
pop: 30 million, half of them Lode contractors
lore: Two continents, two fates: the northern one sold its ore rights to Lode a generation ago, the southern one refused. The ferry between them stopped running the year the mines opened, and families on both shores have not spoken since.

w: cold airless rocky world, the eleventh planet of a dim star
s: dull blue-grey
lore: The eleventh planet of a dim star, cold and airless. A Republic radio relay still broadcasts the Republic's last public notice on a loop, and the few locals live in its buried bunkers and keep it repaired out of stubbornness.

w: ice world of glaciers, bitter cold
s: brilliant white with blue crevasses
m: one small moon, a captured rock
lore: Ice-cutters quarry glaciers and ship them as water to desert worlds, and live in a town cut into the ice itself. The guild keeps its dead frozen into the walls of the town hall, so every meeting is held in front of the people who built it.

w: radioactive wasteland, once jungle
s: dull grey-brown with dead river scars
lore: A jungle world poisoned in the Republic's last war; nothing has grown here since, and the river beds lie dry. Runners hide in the fallout because survey scanners go blind there, and a few scavenger crews work the dead cities in sealed suits.

w: rocky world under a toxic ammonia air, its people under great glass domes
s: pale yellow haze over dark rock, glittering domes
lore: Nobody can breathe its ammonia air, so its people live under great glass domes. Each dome votes every year on how many children it can afford air for, and the result is posted on the dome wall.

w: warm jungle world of caves, rivers and waterfalls
s: rich green with white waterfall mists, mine scars along the valleys
lore: Lode's gem holding, jungle valleys over deep caves of rubies and sapphires. Miners swallow a dye tablet at every shift so stolen stones can be traced; it stains their teeth blue for life, and across the sector blue teeth mean this world.

w: frozen glacier world, thin air
s: blinding white with faint blue seams
lore: A Praevisio vault buried under a glacier, holding the backup ledger of every Birth Debt in the region. Two thousand staff tend it from heated galleries in the ice through winters with no ships; the Unruled would trade a fleet to burn it.

w: gas giant, violent storms
s: deep indigo with white storm spots and a wide faint ring of ice dust
m: dozens of small moons; the five biggest are a geysering ice moon that feeds a wide faint ring, three captured rocks and one dark ice-rock; one moon-fed ice ring
pop: 5,000 skimmer crews in hangar towns riding the equatorial jet
lore: Its skimmer crews live in hangar towns that ride the equatorial jet round the planet, and race the storm bands for bets. The winners fly for the Runners, the losers fly for Lode.

w: unbreathable storm world of bare dry mountain spires
s: purple-grey dust storms over grey needle spires
pop: 30,000 mast climbers in sealed huts on the spires
lore: Rare gases are drawn from the lightning-charged storms by masts on needle-thin mountain spires, and the crews live in sealed huts bolted to the rock below them. Mast crews are paid by the strike: a good year is a short life.

w: airless rocky world of hills and rock stacks; the mud fields are farmed under domes
s: brown and grey, dotted with the grey blisters of the mud domes
lore: When a hand defaults to the Collective, Continuity transfers the balance to their nearest relative and relocates the relative here. The mud fields under the domes are worked by mothers, brothers and children of people who ran.

w: airless rocky world inside Lode's toll ring
s: grey rock circled by a bright orbital ring of docks
pop: 1 million hands, mostly Contract grade, most of them living in the ring
lore: Lode's toll ring on the Charter Road, built round a dead rock; its crews live in the ring itself. Toll is charged by mass, so crews weigh their own dead and put them out of the airlock before the ring to save on the fee.

w: gas giant; the banking houses' garden cities float at the breathable layer
s: soft blue and cream bands, calm
pop: 6 billion free citizens in floating cities
lore: A rich free world whose banking houses sit in terraced garden cities held up by vacuum cells, with vineyards on the upper decks. The banks hold a great deal of Hand debt, which makes it the one free world the Board cannot afford to foreclose, and the bankers know it to the decimal.

w: warm dry world of red clay hills
s: rust red and ochre
lore: A painters' colony in the red clay hills, its towns cut into the clay against the heat. The painters make Alma's adverts by day for money and paint them over by night, and Alma pays them to paint them again in the morning.

w: pale gas giant; the herders live on its big living moon of savanna
s: ochre and white bands, with a yellow-green moon beside it
m: two moons: a large living moon of yellow savanna and green river lines, and a small grey rock
r: cattle, salt beef, hides from the living moon
pop: 5 million herders on the living moon
lore: Herders ride the endless savanna of the giant's living moon, and their cattle are the best-fed meat on the rim. The Collective's fleet eats it salted, and Lode's agents pay twice the price to keep it away from them.

w: warm ocean world of shallow seas and coral reefs
s: turquoise shallows with pale reef rings
m: one small moon, a grey cratered rock
lore: A tiny settlement on stilts over the reef that desalinates water and sells it to passing Runners. The reef is the only thing here older than the colony, and the settlers will shoot anyone who drops anchor on it.

w: tidally locked world; deserts, caves and swamps along the twilight band, lava fields on the day side
s: a sand and rust twilight belt with green swamp patches, a black-red day face and a white night face
m: three moons: one sulphur-yellow, one grey rock, one small captured rock
lore: Seven clans share the swamps and caves of the twilight band, quarry ice on the night side and dig tool-metal from the day side's lava fields. Alma opened a free clinic here, and the births registered there carry Birth Debts the clans can't collect, so Alma sells the debts on.

w: the largest rock of a belt of hollowed rocks round a small orange star
s: glittering grey rock in a faint ring of belt dust, an orange star beyond
m: four captured rocks drawn from the belt, and a faint ring of belt dust
lore: A belt of hollowed rocks round a small orange star, the best repair stop in the sector; the biggest rock holds the pressure docks. Rocks belong to whoever lands on them first and can still hold them a month later.

w: dry blighted farm world, its soil slowly recovering under Grower grain
s: brown fields slowly turning green
m: one moon, a grey cratered rock
pop: 2 million farmers, many of them Growers
lore: Lode abandoned its farms here after a blight and left the soil dead. Growers moved in and bred a blight-proof grain themselves, and the green spreads a few fields further each year; now Lode wants the seed back.

w: tidally locked world; a day face of flare-fused glass plains, a settled twilight band
s: a dazzling white-gold day face with mirror flashes, a thin brown twilight band and a dark night face
m: three small moons: two grey rocks and one cream ice
lore: The day face was fused to glass by a stellar flare a thousand years ago. Lensmakers live in the twilight band, cross into the glare in shuttered crawlers to cut lenses from the plains, and cool the stock on the night side; every lensmaker is half blind by forty.

w: rainy world of marsh plains, bare rock and caves
s: grey-green under heavy cloud
m: one barren moon, a grey cratered rock
lore: Forgers in its caves sell clean Hand numbers to anyone running from a debt. The Hand lets them work, because Praevisio tracks every number they sell.

w: cool rocky world with air still too thin to breathe; farm families building soil on bare stone
s: grey stone with pale green field patches
lore: The air is still too thin to breathe, so families grow moss and grain under long glass sheds and wait for it to thicken. Every field was cleared of stone by hand, and every wall carries the names of the family that cleared it; the oldest farms are fenced with their dead.

w: volcanic island world with freshwater oceans and sulphur haze
s: deep blue sea with smoking black islands
lore: Its oceans are fresh water, rare enough that Lode's tankers come every season to buy. They go home empty: the island councils sell only by the bucket, to people who carry it themselves.

w: hot desert world of named dunes and rock ridges
s: pale sand with dark rock ridges
m: one moon, a pale cratered rock
lore: Desert families who read the dunes: every dune has a name and moves on a known schedule, and caravans pay a dune-reader to guide them. Lode's mapping drones get the dunes wrong every year.

w: warm world of murky jungle and swamp
s: dark green with brown rivers
lore: Its swamp companies fight for Continuity one season and the Runners the next. They keep a scoreboard of both contracts on the same tavern wall.

w: volcanic world of seven great refinery cities, hot and smoky
s: black and red with glowing city grids
lore: Seven fuel refineries, each a sealed city on cooled lava, run by seven families. Its only law is that no family may own two, and every family is always trying.

w: dry world of rocky desert and spreading irrigated farm basins
s: tan desert with bright green basins
m: three moons: two grey rocks and one cream ice
lore: Irrigated farms spread a little further across the desert basins every year, under three moons. Lode bought the water rights through a shell company last year, and the farmers only learned of it when the canals started billing them.

w: temperate world of countryside and plateaus
s: soft green and gold
lore: A rolling green world that trades with nobody. Visitors are met at the landing field with a meal and a full tank, and politely asked to leave by nightfall.

w: barren airless rock strewn with rusting hulls
s: dull tan rock scattered with rusting hulls
lore: A barren airless rock where Lode parks freighters it has written off but not yet sold. Scrapper families seal the hulls and live in them rent-free until Lode remembers them, and some are on their third generation.

w: hot airless rock of gem diggings
s: sandy orange rock under five moons
m: five moons: grey rock, dark ice-rock, sulphur-yellow, a captured rock and cream ice
lore: A dry airless rock of gem diggers who live down their own shafts and trade stones for shipped-in water. A cup costs a cut gem, so nobody here wears jewellery.

w: rocky world whose ozone was stripped by a failed terraform
s: bleached white and pale brown
lore: A terraforming job went wrong and stripped the ozone: the noon sun burns skin in minutes. Its people live in tunnel towns and go out only at night; they say 'good night' when they meet and 'good day' when they part.

w: cold airless rocky world, unlived on except for its graveyards
s: dark grey, circled by a ring of parked hulls
m: no moons; a ring of stolen ore haulers parked in orbit
pop: 60,000 Dust, all living in the parked haulers
lore: Dust families who walked out on Lode live in the hulls of the ore haulers they stole, still parked nose to tail in a ring around the planet. They come down only to bury their dead.

w: hot airless rock, cratered; the Runner town is cut into the north cliffs under pressure doors
s: grey-brown cratered rock, one bright point of light on the north cliffs
m: three moons: a cratered rock, a dark ice-rock and a captured lump
r: fuel, ship repairs, hidden cargo, pilots
lore: The Runners' capital at the far end of the fastest unpaid lane in the galaxy, a path through gravity wells only Runner pilots can fly. A beacon burns on the north cliffs over the sealed town; a pilot who makes it in gets a drink, a berth and no questions.

w: searing world of swamps, rainforests and bogs
s: steaming green with brown rivers
m: three moons: a hazy giant, a cratered rock and a captured lump
lore: A searing swamp world whose cooks turn insects and fungus into the rations that feed half the Collective's fleet. Every ship's galley swears by a different recipe, and fights have started over less.

w: varied temperate world scarred by abandoned Lode mines
s: blue and green with grey abandoned mine scars
lore: Thirty years ago the workers of a Lode holding walked off the job and never went back. The Locals run it as a planned commune, and the Unruled keep blowing up the plans.

w: temperate world turned desert: dead forest and bare plains where the soil washed away
s: pale tan with grey ghost-forests
m: three moons: a cratered rock, a dark ice-rock and a captured lump
lore: Lode strip-logged the rainforest for pit props and left, and the rains washed the soil away within a single lifetime. The settlers sued in the Republic's last court and are still waiting for a ruling.

w: temperate coastal world, mild climate
s: soft blue sea and green shore under light cloud
lore: The Collective's largest dry house: a whole quiet coast of beds facing the sea, where recruits come off Alma's pill. When they can stand again, they choose a new name, and the coast throws a party for every one.

w: world of mountains, rainforests and salt marshes
s: white salt flats between green mountains and dark sea
lore: The Unwritten bring every machine they capture here and smash it on the salt flats. After two centuries the flats glitter with broken circuitry, and pilgrims walk across them barefoot.

w: pale blue-green gas giant with eighteen moons; the raft towns float on the seas of the largest, a warm living moon of rainforest, swamp, ocean and volcanoes
s: a blue-green banded giant; its big living moon shows green and blue with white surf
m: eighteen moons; the five biggest drawn: the living moon, a volcanic moon, a smooth ice moon, a cratered rock and a captured lump
pop: 20 million raft-town folk on the living moon
lore: Eighteen moons pull at the living moon's seas, and its tides are impossible to predict. The raft-town fishermen publish a tide almanac every year and are wrong every year, and betting on it is the moon's favourite pastime.

w: volcanic world of jutting obsidian crags, vents still glowing between them
s: glossy black with grey ash plains and thin orange cracks
lore: Obsidian crags, still warm, knapped by hand into blades and mirrors. The Runners' moneychangers live in sealed cliff houses above the vents and keep the Collective's only accounts: the one set of books nobody wants burned.

w: ocean world, warm, scattered small islands
s: deep blue with white reef rings around the islands
m: five small moons: three cratered rock and two captured rock
pop: 2 million islanders in seven island federations
lore: Island villages on an endless sea refuse to build a spaceport: ships must splash down offshore and be towed in by rowing crews, at a rowing crew's pace. The Hand's survey ships have waited a week for a tow and gone home.

w: hot, humid swamp world under steady rain
s: olive and brown, wrapped in thick white cloud
pop: 6 billion free citizens, runaways and clan families
lore: The elder of the twin free ports, run by the Weighhouse, a guild of founding clans. Its law has one line the Hand hates: a Birth Debt dies at the dock. Any hand who lands here is free, so the Board pays the Weighhouse yearly to send runaways back, and it sends most of them.

w: gas giant hidden in grey-white fog
