s: a smear of grey-white haze over faint dark green bands
m: three small moons, all captured rock
r: hired labour, smoked goods, fuel gas
lore: The fog never lifts, and its villages float in it, sinking slowly and burning fuel to climb back, so none is ever where it was. The Hand's census is a guess: whole villages appear on no list, and nobody there was ever billed for being born. The Board's estimate has changed by a million in each of the last five years.

w: city-world, stacked towers, breathable air
s: a blaze of amber city light on the night side, grey towers by day
r: markets, forged identities, ship refits, everything stolen
pop: 80 billion free citizens, runaways and traders
lore: Vrijhaven's younger twin: a whole world of towers stacked by the same founding clans. Vrijhaven keeps the law, Hoogstad keeps the market, and anything can be bought here, including a dead hand's number. By treaty no Continuity soldier may carry a weapon past the quay; Continuity is counting the days.

w: cold airless rocky world
s: dull brown with pale dust plains
lore: A bare rock where convoys bound for the twin free ports gather before the last jump, and the mooring families live in pressurised sheds by the pads. Every captain who musters here leaves a stone on the cairn by the landing field; the cairn is now taller than the control tower.

w: cool forest world, long mild summers
s: pale silver-green, white birch bark visible along the river valleys
lore: Birch forests settled by families who plant a tree for every child born. Alma's analysts have started counting the trees from orbit to estimate the births they are not billing.

w: airless rocky moonlet with a pressurised dock
s: dark grey speck with a ring of dock lights
lore: A refuelling stop between the free ports and the Hand's lanes, its crews living in the pressurised dock. By old custom anyone who fires a weapon here is barred by every captain in the sector, for life, and the custom has held for ninety years.

w: irradiated volcanic world of lava plains and steaming rifts, near-constant rain
s: sullen red glow under a grey steam haze
r: guards for hire, heavy ore, hardy fruit
lore: An old Republic reactor burst here before the Receivership and the ground still smoulders. The people live in sealed towns and sell their young as guards to the free ports; few on Scaldwell live past fifty, so they sign up young and send the money home.

w: a built habitat ring round its star, spun for gravity, never finished
s: a dull-gold band round its star, flashing as it turns, long stretches of hull still bare
m: none (a built ring round its star)
lore: A Republic bank began this ring round its star and went bust before it was paid for, long before the Hand. Legally it belongs to the Board. For two hundred years its three hundred million squatters have kept it turning and voted once a year not to answer the letters.

w: temperate world, several continents of varied climate
s: blue seas and patchwork green-gold continents
lore: A quiet farming world whose council has twice voted to join the Hand, for the clinics and the freighters, and twice been talked out of it by the grandmothers who remember what the clinics cost.

w: hot desert world of salt pans
s: blinding white flats edged with tan dunes
lore: Salt flats walked by caravans of crawlers that sell to whoever lands; the families live aboard the crawlers and never stop moving. They have no government and no word for one; a dispute is settled by walking apart.

w: temperate world of endless plains
s: gold and green bands under thin cloud
pop: 7 billion farmers in a planet-wide cooperative
lore: Seven billion farmers feed half the sector. The planetary grain cooperative sells to Lode at a fixed price every year, and the Hand buys rather than takes, as long as the price stays low enough.

w: olive gas giant; the clan villages are on its two living moons
s: olive and brown bands beside two green moons
m: two living moons of forest and cropland
pop: 500 million clan villagers on the two moons
lore: Clan villages cover two living moons of forest and cropland, and the chiefs sell their own people's labour contracts to Lode by the shipload. The Hand never had to conquer Clanmoor; it only had to keep buying.

w: tropical world of jungle islands, mountains and swamp
s: emerald islands in a turquoise sea, brown silt plumes along the coasts
lore: Jungle islands whose mangrove mud holds a rare earth Lode wants. The island chiefs license the dredging one island at a time, and each island blames the next for the dead shallows.

w: tidally locked desert world; mirror fields cover the day face
s: tan day face with vast flashing mirror fields, a dark frozen night side
lore: Republic-era solar mirrors still cover a third of the burning day face and beam power to whoever pays. The mirror families live in the twilight, cut their water from the night-side ice, and have kept the mirrors running for two hundred years without a spare part they did not make themselves.

w: toxic world of poison yellow air left by a failed atmosphere job; nine sealed domes in one valley
s: mustard-yellow haze with dark valley scars
lore: A Republic atmosphere job went wrong here and left air nobody can breathe. Nine sealed domes share one air plant in a poisoned valley; whoever holds the valves runs the planet, and the valves have changed hands four times in ten years.

w: temperate world of rolling hills
s: green and blue under light cloud
pop: 20 million, many still paying an old clinic debt
lore: A fever emptied this world eighty years ago. Alma's clinics arrived, cured it, and sent the survivors the bill. Their grandchildren live on a free world and still pay it every month.

w: cool world of bare pink rock under a thin breathable air nobody finished
s: pinkish-grey rock with white station lights
pop: 2 million Contract-grade toll staff and families
lore: Somebody gave this rock breathable air and never got round to soil or water, so nothing grows. Lode's toll station sits on it at the edge of the free ports. Every hold that passes is opened and searched, and confiscated cargo is auctioned the same day.

w: cold world of dark forest and still frozen lakes
s: dark green and black, frozen lakes like mirrors
lore: A cold, quiet world where trappers live beside a few thousand Kiru exiles. The Hand has offered the trappers free relocation to a core holding, the Kiru not included. So far nobody has signed.

w: dry stripped world; topsoil and young forest regrowing on the old mine pits, terraforming under way
s: rust-orange pits patched with green
lore: Lode stripped this world sixty years ago and left. Grower communes have built topsoil a metre deep on the old pit floors, and over the greenest pits the rain has started to come back. Lode has just filed to re-survey it.

w: cold high moors, frozen most of the year, deep valleys with silver lakes
s: grey-green moor under frost, silver lakes, white uplands
lore: Once a year rival Unwritten sects meet here in truce. No machine more complicated than a pump may land, and the villagers turn out every pilgrim's pockets at the field.

w: temperate world of oceans, forests, mountains and plains
s: deep blue seas, green lands, white peaks
lore: Alma's scouts rated Highmere the finest rest world in the sector. Its people have declined Alma's offer three times; the fourth offer is expected with a fleet.

w: tidally locked world; tawny grass plains in the twilight band, swept by cool dry winds
s: tawny-red grass ring between a cracked day face and a frozen night face, clear skies
lore: Herders graze the twilight grass, bury their dead in the night-side ice and never cross into the burnt day side. They count their wealth in animals, not money, so Lode's freight agents must barter: one crate of tools for so many head of cattle, a rate unchanged in eighty years.

w: desert world with sprawling factory cities
s: beige desert with dense grey city grids
lore: Desert factory cities that build dumb, sturdy machines with no thinking core, to a standard written so the Unwritten would let them live. The Unwritten bombed two factories anyway. Praevisio buys the output and adds the thinking itself.

w: temperate forest world
s: deep green forest under white cloud
lore: Lumber towns cut the dark forests and sell hardwood to the Hand for Board yachts. Each town elects a sheriff, and none of them answers to any other.

w: gas giant; skimmer families' scoop rafts drift her equator in season, homes on five moons
s: banded cream and soft orange, swirling storms, a faint dust ring
m: five inhabited moons and a faint dust ring
pop: 6 million on five moons, and the skimming crews on their rafts in season
lore: The settlers of five moons call the gas giant Grandmother and skim her clouds for fuel each season from drifting scoop rafts. By moon custom nobody may marry inside their own moon, so every wedding is a voyage, and most are arranged on the rafts.

w: arctic world of ice cliffs and cold seas
s: brilliant white with blue-black seas
lore: Its cities are cut into ice cliffs, and the ice is retreating. Each decade another city slides into the sea, and the Hand offers relocation to its holdings, at a price.

w: desert world, hot days, freezing nights
s: ochre and red desert, dark mountain ridges
lore: An old Republic penal colony whose prisoners were forgotten at the Receivership. Their great-grandchildren run it as a free world of former convicts, and are very proud of it.

w: airless rocky world under nightly meteor falls; the towns are underground
s: grey-blue cratered world under a broken glittering ring
m: one remnant moonlet inside a broken ring of rock debris
lore: What is left of a shattered moon circles the planet and rains stone every night onto a world with no air to burn it. The settlers live underground and come up at dawn to sweep the streets of meteorite iron, which they sell.

w: temperate world of lakes, swamps and forests in dense fog
s: grey fog over dark green and silver water
lore: A world of lakes and fog where every crossing belongs to the ferrymen's guild. The guild has never once carried a Hand surveyor across.

w: temperate world of savannas, forests and mountains
s: golden savanna and dark forest under thin cloud
lore: An old Republic beacon still guides every ship on the western routes, and whoever controls it controls the west. The hereditary keepers will not sell, and have turned down the Hand, the Runners and the Collective in the same year.

w: green-gold gas giant; the distilleries are on its two living moons
s: soft green-gold bands, with two small green-and-blue moons beside them
m: two living moons of orchards and small seas
pop: 68 million settlers on the two moons
lore: Its two living moons are orchard country, and their distilleries make a pear spirit the Board drinks. The distiller families enjoy a quiet exemption from Lode's tolls as long as the bottles keep coming; the year a crop failed, Lode sent an auditor instead of a freighter.

w: last charted gas giant in the west; one drifting town rides its winds
s: green-grey bands pocked with dark round storms
m: two moons: a dark ice-rock and a small captured rock
pop: 200,000 townsfolk and drifters on one drifting raft town
lore: The last charted world in the west. Its one town is a raft that drifts with the wind, and the wells it lowers into the deep cloud for water and fuel belong to whoever holds them this week. Beyond it the Hand's maps go blank, and the town sells charts of the dark that nobody can check.

w: rugged frozen mountain world
s: grey-brown peaks over snowbound white valleys
pop: 900 million mountain clans in fortress towns
lore: Nine mountain warlords have been at war for forty years from fortress towns cut into the snowbound valleys. Continuity sells guns to all nine and counts on the war never ending.

w: desert and dry forest world under a crowded sky
s: tan deserts and dark forests under a broken ring of debris
m: five moons, the smallest half-mined and trailing a debris ring of the five that were mined to rubble
pop: 15 million settlers in towns dug in under rock roofs
lore: It had ten moons. Lode mined five of them to rubble on an old contract, and the debris ring still sheds burning stones on the towns, which are dug in under rock roofs. The settlers pray at night for a clear sky.

w: hot desert world
s: bright yellow sand with dark glassworks
lore: Desert glassworks melt sand into viewport glass, worked at night because the day kills. Middlemen sell it to Mordant at a cut rate, and every Mandate's bridge window may have started here.

w: bare rocky world with thin breathable air; survivors are greening its river valleys
s: grey rock with green threads along deep river valleys
lore: Survivors of a harvested human system live here, coaxing moss and grass up the deep river valleys of a bare rock that barely holds its air. They keep the harvest notice framed in their meeting hall, and read it aloud on the anniversary.

w: murky gas giant; the swamp clans live on its living moon of jungles, swamps and murky seas
s: an olive and brown banded giant, and beside it a deep green moon with murky seas
m: four moons: the living swamp moon and three small rocks
pop: 1.3 billion swamp-clan citizens on the living moon
lore: Swamp clans on the green moon train the best trackers on the rim, hunting each other through the mangroves for practice. Many of the Hand's Repossessors learned their trade here, and the clans take a fee for every one they train.

w: rocky world of glittering quartz plains packed with city-states
s: sparkling white and pale blue, lights in dozens of separate clusters
lore: The largest free world on the old trunk route: dozens of city-states packed onto the quartz plains. Lode's toll lane runs straight through, and every year the cities vote on whether to pay.

w: grey-blue gas giant; garrison decks ride a permanent rain belt at the breathable layer
s: grey-blue bands under endless cloud, one darker rain belt round the middle
m: two moons, a grey rock and a hazy orange giant
pop: 150 million Contract and Indentured grade on the barrack decks, most in Tranches
lore: A gas giant where Tranche regiments are formed and drilled on barrack decks that ride one rain belt round the planet and never leave it. The soldiers call it the Wet. The decks have not been dry in eighty years, and recruits are told the rot is part of the training.

w: desert world over deep fossil ice aquifers
s: pale tan with frost rings round the shafts
pop: 300 million shaft families in towns built round the wellheads
lore: Under the desert lies an ocean of fossil ice. The families who own the shafts sell water to three sectors, and Lode wants the shafts.

w: dry mountain world of deep canyons with green floors
s: red-brown canyons with thin green floors
m: two moons, one grey and one a small captured rock
lore: Canyon towns where the Unruled once burned a debt registry. They keep the ashes in a jar at the canyon's mouth.

w: temperate world of reed swamps, wet meadows and forest
s: green with silver wetlands
m: two moons, one grey and one of white ice
lore: A few fishing villages in the reed swamps who have never met a Hand official. Their only outside visitor is a Collective midwife, twice a year.

w: desert world on the long shore of a dried-up sea
s: yellow sand meeting a grey-white salt basin where the ocean was
lore: A dead shoreline at the junction of two lanes, where Lode freighters dump ballast water to lighten up for the climb. It falls as brief rain on the old sea bed. The coast towns live on what spills out, and distil brandy from the scrub that blooms after.

w: warm world of flower fields
s: pale violet fields under thin cloud
lore: Fields of the pale flower from which Alma's happiness pill is made. The growers sell every bloom, and none of them takes the pill.

w: barren rock with thin breathable air; the air was made, the soil never took
s: bleached grey, faint stripes of dead seeding grids, a thin blue rim of air
lore: A Republic-era telescope on a rock whose air was made breathable two centuries ago. Nothing ever grew in it, and the dead seeding grids still stripe the plains. The astronomers who refuse to leave see farther than Praevisio's probes, and sell what they see.

w: airless rocky world whose dried-up sea left long iron-sand beaches
s: grey-black iron-sand shores around pale, dry sea beds
pop: 1 million sand dredgers in sealed crawler towns
lore: The sea boiled off long ago and left its beaches. Free crews dredge the iron sand from sealed crawler towns that roll along the old shoreline, and sell it to Mordant for Hand scrip they can spend only at Hand stations. The crews call the scrip sand, too.

w: cool grey-green gas giant; the old hunting forests grow on its large living moon
s: muted grey-green bands, and beside them a forest moon under heavy cloud
m: three moons: a living forest moon, a dark ice-rock and a small captured rock
r: venison, timber; a little fuel gas skimmed for the lodges
pop: 2 million gamekeepers' families on the forest moon
lore: The forest moon's grey woods were old Republic hunting estates. The gamekeepers' descendants still keep the deer for owners dead two centuries, and shoot trespassers. The giant overhead they leave alone; the lodges call it the Landlord.

w: hot junk world where Mordant's molten slag pools under acid rain
s: rust-brown and black scrap mountains cracked with orange slag glow under brown smoke
pop: 4 million salvagers in towns dug under cooled heaps
lore: Mordant's waste world: slag, spoiled alloy and failed castings are dropped here from orbit, and glow for years where they land. Salvage clans live in towns dug under the cooled heaps and pick through the rest in the acid rain. A third of the Collective's fighters started out as something Mordant threw away.

w: dry tan gas giant whose one forested moon is the only living place in the system
s: bare tan-brown bands beside a bright green moon
lore: The only living place in the system is the giant's forest moon, where tappers bleed a resin that Alma uses in its cosmetics. Alma pays by the barrel, and sets the size of the barrel each season.

w: ocean world
s: deep blue with green kelp swirls
lore: A sea world whose kelp feeds the whole sector. A quarter of its seas belong to Lode on a lease a drunk mayor signed eighty years ago, and Lode's kelp barges fly no town's flag.

w: hot desert world
s: orange desert with black refinery stacks
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a small captured rock
pop: 150,000 Dust families in cellars under the refineries
lore: Lode abandoned the refineries here. Dust families moved in and run them for the Collective; the furnace has not gone cold in eleven years. The families sleep in cellars cut under the stacks, the one place the desert heat lets up.

w: airless rock with a pressurised quay
s: dark rock lit by a string of dock lamps
pop: 20,000 dockers in the quay's pressure halls
lore: A Runner waystation on an airless rock where crews leave their dead in a sealed vault, so no body can be traced back to a ship. The dockers live in the pressure halls beside it. The vault is nearly full, and nobody has agreed whose dead move out.

w: toxic marsh world; one sprawling stilt city over a poisoned delta
s: black water and grey city sprawl along one delta, under yellow-grey haze
pop: 700 million marsh-city residents, packed on one delta
lore: A city on stilts over the poisoned marsh of a dead Republic chemical works, its towers sealed against the air. The Hand won't take it because the clean-up would cost more than the yield, and the residents know their poison is their armour.

w: temperate world of hills, plains and clinic cities
s: soft green and white, clinic cities glinting
m: three moons: two grey rocks and one pale ice
pop: 4 billion hands, mostly clinic staff and contract mothers
lore: Alma's cheapest birth clinic world. Mothers from thirty holdings are flown in to give birth here, because Alma's licence fees are lowest; Alma calls it the Cradle.

w: jungle world under heavy rain, with server vaults under the canopy
s: deep green with silver server roofs
m: two moons, one grey rock, one dark ice-rock
pop: 300 Praevisio technicians on rotation, 40,000 maintenance drones
lore: A Praevisio data vault cooled by jungle rain. Three hundred technicians rotate through on six-month contracts; the drones tend the servers and the jungle, and nobody asks for a second rotation.

w: snow world of cold grey seas and snow beaches
s: white with grey-blue seas
m: one moon, a grey cratered rock
lore: Snow beaches where hunters cut ice-fish from holes in the sea ice and live in snow-banked turf villages. The village elders have refused Hand clinics three times, and their children are born at home.

w: dry savanna world of tawny grass and watering holes
s: tawny grass with dark watering holes
m: three moons: two grey rocks and one small captured rock
lore: The Hand's border fence ends here: a line of sensor posts across the savanna. The herders cut it every dry season and the Hand repairs it every wet one.

w: temperate world of hills and oceans, landscaped by Alma
s: blue seas and soft green hills
lore: An executive rest world that Alma landscaped from bare hills: every lawn and shoreline was laid by contract. Nothing is made here; everything is imported, including the smiles, and the staff are kept on the pill.

w: mountain world of snowfields and high pastures
s: grey peaks and snowfields with green high pastures
lore: Mountain herders hire out to Lode on fixed ten-year terms. The Hand honours the terms only because it needs their climbers, and they come home.

w: cold, near-airless rocky world with a long crash scar
s: grey with a long dark crash scar
pop: 40,000 settlers and a few hundred Nhal
lore: A small Nhal family group lives in the sealed wreck of the ark that crashed bringing them here. The human settlers built their pressure town round it and grow crops in its shadow.

w: scorched wasteland of mountains, still smouldering where the forests burned
s: black and grey scorched lands with dull red seams
lore: A crop blight nobody could stop burned its forests two centuries before the Receivership, and the peat beneath still smoulders. Scavengers live in sealed ruins and wear masks outdoors; Alma's broadcasts show those ruins as proof of what happens to a world nobody manages.

w: blue-green methane gas giant; trawler towns drift on rafts across its dense lower cloud
s: blue-green bands with bright flares where the raft towns burn off gas
pop: 800 million trawler families in thousands of drifting raft towns
lore: Trawler towns drift on rafts across the dense lower cloud like boats on a sea, burning off spare gas in flares you can see from orbit. They sell fuel to every ship on the trunk route, Hand or not, at the same price: their neutrality is the price list.

w: airless rocky world of frost-cracked cliffs; clan villages in sealed galleries cut into the seams
s: pale gold with lilac quartz scars
lore: Settler families cut singing quartz from the cliff seams and live in sealed galleries behind it. Each family's seam map is tattooed on the eldest daughter's back. When a Lode surveyor photographed one at a wedding, the family closed the seam with explosives that same night.

w: hot volcanic world; jungle mesas terraced into fields above smoking valleys of live lava
s: brick-red and deep green mesas, smoke plumes and glowing valley floors
m: three moons, one used as Lode's grain silo
r: stim-leaf, hardwood, rare earths from the valley floors
pop: 1.5 billion hands, mostly Contract and Indentured grade
lore: Lode's plantation holding: brick-red jungle mesas terraced into stim-leaf fields above valleys of live lava. Pickers are paid by the basket and fined by the bruise, and the mesa towns are named for the year each was cleared.

w: hot salt flats and red canyons, a few shallow brine pans
s: blinding white pans veined with rust-red canyons
lore: A white salt-pan world under one hard sun, held by the Margrave family under a deed older than the Receivership. Lode has offered to buy it seven times; each refusal is read aloud in the square on its anniversary.

w: hot dry world of mesas and dust plains; sealed domes and unlit foundry halls
s: ochre plains stitched with white foundry blocks
m: fifteen captured moonlets, three hollowed into data vaults
r: war robots, Gleaner drones, servo parts
lore: Praevisio's largest robot foundry: Proxies walk off the line here by the regiment. The last human shift was separated ahead of schedule eleven years ago, and the floors have run unlit ever since, because nothing on them needs to see.

w: wet, empty proving ground: rain-soaked uplands, bogs and small seas
s: slate-blue seas and dark green bog under grey rain bands
r: test ranges, salvage from wrecked robots
pop: 12,000 range staff plus whichever Tranche is on trial
lore: A wet, empty proving ground where Continuity matches Tranche squads against Praevisio's Proxies in live-fire trials. Praevisio publishes the results each quarter; Continuity disputes every one, and the grave terraces keep growing.

w: cold ocean world of rocky islands
s: dark navy sea flecked with grey islands
r: cod-like fish, kelp oil, sea salt
lore: A cold archipelago of fishing clans. For every child taken by Repossessors a family scuttles one of its boats in the harbour, and the oldest harbours are now too shallow to use.

w: frigid world of frozen seas and tundra
s: white and pale blue, almost featureless
lore: When the sea freezes, the ice road joins the islands and the year's only market opens on it for ninety days. Anything still on the ice when it melts belongs to the sea, by custom, so the market's last day is a frantic auction.

w: brown gas giant, banded and stormy; skimmer barges dive its cloud tops
s: tan and umber bands with a dark storm spot, a lit refinery moon
pop: 90,000 hands on the moon refinery and its skimmer barges
lore: A brown gas giant Lode skims for fuel: barges dive from the refinery moon into the cloud tops and climb back full. The moon's crews breathe refinery air and are billed for it per lungful under Lode's atmosphere contract.

w: warm swamp world, river deltas and peat bogs
s: olive-green marsh under constant haze
r: peat fuel, river rice, smuggled goods
lore: Stilt towns over a vast delta of peat and mangrove. The dead are set adrift downriver on lit rafts, and Runners use the burning nights to slip cargo past Hand pickets.

w: hot volcanic world, lava plains and ash, foundries over the vents
s: black and glowing orange, yard lights across the night side
m: two moons, one ringed with dry docks
pop: 1 billion hands, most Indentured yard lifers
lore: Mordant's oldest outer-rim yard, built over lava vents that heat its foundries for free. The shift siren has sounded every eight hours for a hundred and forty years; it stayed silent for one day only, the day of the great walkout at Navalia, when Caminus walked out too.

w: gas giant with permanent storms, ringed with the wreckage of dead skimmer platforms
s: deep cobalt with white lightning flecks and a thin grey ring of wreckage
m: two moons, both bare rock, and a thin ring of wrecked platforms
pop: a few hundred Runners at the last working platform
lore: A violent blue giant where the skimmer platforms abandoned when the gas thinned have fallen into a ring of wreckage. Runners refuel by hand from the last one still floating in the storms, and leave a tally mark for anyone who never came back.

w: gold gas giant with an orbital toll ring round its equator
s: gold-yellow bands behind a ring of station lights
m: none; the toll ring is the only habitation
lore: Lode's toll ring on the trade route: every ship on the lane docks at one of its stations and pays. Toll clerks keep a share of what they collect, so new fees appear every quarter, among them a fee for queueing.

w: dry plains world of golden grassland and shrinking lake beds
s: golden grassland with pale dry lake beds and farm circles
lore: A broad plains world whose assembly is a third Collective sympathisers and a third the Hand's friends. The last third are farmers who vote with the weather, and both sides pray for rain.

w: temperate world, port cities on long coasts
s: green coasts lit up along every harbour
lore: A dock world on the trade route where the Locals run every crane. Hand freighters sit in orbit for weeks when a slowdown is called, and nobody can ever prove that one was.

w: cold rock of bare plateaus with no air worth breathing; prison blocks under pressure roofs
s: dull brown with white prison grids and quarry scars
r: prison labour, quarried stone, uniform cloth
lore: Continuity's labour prison, its blocks sealed under pressure roofs on a rock with no air worth breathing. Sentences are counted in debt, not years, and the debt accrues room, board and air, so most inmates owe more each year they serve.

w: temperate hill world, old stone cities
s: green hills and walled cities
lore: Old banking families who lent the Republic money and lost it at the Receivership. They still hold the notes and sue the Board in Hand courts every year. They always lose, and pay the court fees gladly.

w: warm swamp world of reed marshes
s: bright green reed beds and brown channels
lore: Lode leases the reed-sugar marshes to free cutters at a rate that leaves them exactly even every year. In sixty years nobody has turned a profit, and nobody has quite starved.

w: mild lake world of gentle hills, shaped and dyed by Alma's terraformers
s: vivid blue lakes on soft green
lore: Alma's executive resort, its hills shaped and its lakes dyed a perfect blue by Alma's own terraformers. The staff smile by contract, and guests' children are delivered at the clinic by the shore at a family discount.

w: temperate ocean world, large forested islands
s: deep blue with dark green islands
lore: Forested islands in a deep sea. A small Nhal exile community lives on a raft town off the largest island, and the islanders have quietly sunk two Repossessor boats that came for them.

w: volcanic flatlands, sulphur air, thin oxygen; the farms live under domes
s: mustard-yellow plains cut by glowing lava seams, dotted with white farm domes
lore: Domed fungus farms on sulphur plains where the open air will kill you in an hour, between lava seams that glow red at night. Alma buys half of every crop, and nobody on the farms asks what for.

w: temperate gas giant; a free port rides the breathable layer on rotor platforms
s: tan and sage-green bands under a soft haze, one small cratered moon
m: one small moon, its craters fitted out as refit docks
pop: 9 million, in the floating port and the moon docks
lore: A free port built on a cluster of rotor platforms that hold it in the clouds and never stop turning. Three Runner families take turns ruling for a hundred days each, and at each handover the ruling family burns its ledgers in the market square. Ships too big to come down are refitted in the moon's craters.

w: frigid world of glaciers
s: brilliant white with blue crevasse lines
pop: 20,000 ice-haulers, in heated galleries cut into the glacier
lore: A crevasse on this glacier world holds a Mandate destroyer that crashed forty years ago, nearly intact. The ice-hauling family lives in heated galleries cut beside it, sells salvage rights to both sides and delivers to neither.

w: warm dry savanna world, no seas, rain only in spring
s: tawny plains most of the year, whole continents of orange flowers in spring
lore: Dry savanna ranch country where dye flowers turn whole continents orange each spring and the grass goes back to tawny by summer. The herders keep no money at all and trade only in cattle, which puzzles Hand tax assessors.

w: dry world of deep canyons
s: red-brown with black canyon lines
lore: Canyon towns carved into the walls, out of the sun and the dust. Every nine years a flood scours the canyon floor, and the bottom town is always rebuilt in the same spot, by the same families, out of stubbornness.

w: pale gas giant; its one moon is a small living world, stripped by Lode and grown back
s: a pale gold and cream gas giant, and beside it a small green and gold moon
m: one living moon, regrown fields and young forest
r: new soil, seed crops, timber, all from the moon
lore: Lode stripped the topsoil from this giant's living moon and sold it off-world, and twenty years of rain brought the land back. Eight hundred Growers settled it quietly. Lode's survey still lists the moon as dead, and the Growers mean to keep it that way.

w: temperate world of tidal mudflats and grey shallow seas
s: brown mudflats and grey sea, shifting daily under a huge close moon
lore: A big close moon drags the sea back and forth across the mudflats, and the flats are thick with shellfish. The towns are built on sledges, and each storm season the whole population hauls them inland on ropes.

w: gas giant
s: amber and cream bands with a pale broad ring
m: two moons, both cratered rock, both settled under domes; one pale broad ring
pop: 6 million, on the two moons and the tether barges
lore: Six million skimmer crews live in domes on its two moons and in barges that hang over the clouds, dropping scoops on tethers kilometres long. The moon guilds sell fuel to anyone, the Hand included, and that neutrality is all that protects them.

w: frozen world of ice plains and glaciers, one valley thawing under orbital mirrors
s: white with one dark green-blue valley and a lake
m: three moons: two cratered rock and one captured rock
lore: A Grower commune parked salvaged mirrors in orbit to warm one frozen valley, and lives in greenhouses dug into its walls. After twelve years there is a lake where there was a glacier, and the first barley. The rest of the world is still ice.

w: gas giant on the Trunk Line, ringed by the wreck of a toll gate
s: dusty green and grey bands, a glittering wreck ring in orbit
m: one moon, cratered rock; one wreck ring made of the old toll gate
r: free passage, gate salvage, fuel gas
pop: 800,000 in refloated hulls in the clouds
lore: The Unruled blew up Lode's toll gate here; its wreck still tumbles round the giant as a glittering ring. The salvagers live in the gate's old tender hulls, kept afloat in the clouds by heating gas in their fuel tanks. Ships have passed the Trunk Line here free ever since, and Lode has sworn to rebuild the gate.

w: dry world of deserts and mountains, full gravity
s: tan deserts and grey peaks
lore: Dust families who left their rocks for a dry mountain world, and dug their towns into the peaks out of habit. Adults still walk with braces under full gravity; their children are the first Dust who can run.

w: cool airless rocky world of quarried hills
s: grey and white, terraced quarries
lore: Free quarrymen cut the grey granite that faces the Board's own towers on Charter, and live in pressurised halls cut into the quarry terraces. They are paid in full and on time, and the Hand forgives them a great deal for it.

w: gas giant; seven free cities ride the rising columns of warm gas
s: grey-gold bands with five pale storm spots
pop: 5 billion city dwellers in seven floating cities
lore: Seven floating cities, each as wide as a continent, ride the warm updrafts of a gas giant and hire out five billion workers by the shift to Hand holdings. The contract renewal each year is the cities' real election, and their Locals sit at the table.

w: hot barren plains with scattered oases
s: red-ochre plains, the oases too small to see from orbit
lore: Oasis cities linked by caravan across hot red plains, each green round its own well. Each oasis sells its red pigment dust; feuds between wells are older than the Hand.

w: cold airless rocky world, one walled town under a pressure dome
s: dull grey with one bright town
lore: A walled town under a pressure dome that rents prison cells to anyone, by the night. Repossessors lodge their catches here on the way to the market at Tallow Mesa, and the cell-keepers are known for feeding everyone the same.

w: temperate world, rolling orchards
s: bright blue skies over green and pink
lore: Orchard towns of a quiet faith that buries every machine it uses underground. Unwritten pilgrims come to admire it and are turned away for being too loud.

w: toxic desert of rusted factory plains under polluted air
s: brown smog over dark rust plains, factory scars and burning stacks
m: one moon, a grey cratered rock
r: scrap, machine parts, cheap industrial goods
lore: An abandoned factory world Lode walked away from. A million scavengers live in the sealed factory halls, breathe through filters and run machines nobody pays for; the stacks still burn because nobody remembers how to shut them down.

w: cool shallow-water world of reed islands and fish weirs
s: grey-green shallows dotted with reed islands under low cloud
lore: Every family runs a fish weir from its own reed island and has a vote, and children join the council at ten. The fish go out on Collective ships, and the Hand fines the weirs when it can find them.

w: frigid world of snowfields and dark pine forest, with nine-year winters
s: white with dark red-brown forest belts and frozen grey seas
lore: Winter here lasts nine years. Families sleep through the dark in shared longhouses dug half into the frozen ground, and wake each spring to count who did not.

w: temperate upland world of wheat plateaus and small seas
s: golden fields under clear skies, small blue seas
lore: Free wheat farmers who must sell to Lode at Lode's price, because Lode owns the only lane out. They feed half the sector and cannot afford new boots.

w: pale gas giant with a calm trading band; a market town floats in it under gas bags
s: olive and cream bands, a busy orbit of traders round a lit dock ring at the equator
pop: 25 million traders on the floating market and its dock ring
lore: A market town hangs under a crown of giant gas bags in the calm band, on the Trunk Line. A bronze bell rung there at dawn sets every price; anyone may ring it once in their life, and the day's prices are theirs.

w: airless rocky world inside a ring of wrecked warships
s: grey cratered world under a glittering ring of wrecks
m: no moons; a glittering ring of wrecked ships
lore: A ring of wrecked ships from a battle nobody now remembers circles this airless rock. One large family of scrappers picks it over and lives in pressurised hulls hauled down to the surface; they sell to anyone and remember everyone.

w: temperate industrial world of strike-held cities and green belts
s: grey cities with green between them, blue seas
m: one moon, a grey cratered rock
lore: The Locals called a general strike here eleven years ago and never ended it. The Hand's managers left, and the strike committees now run the whole world, factory by factory.

w: airless rocky world between two jump points too close to jump between
s: brown and grey-green rock with ferry lights on the night side
lore: Two jump points on the Trunk Line sit too close to jump between, so ferry clans tow ships across from buried hangar towns on this airless rock. They charge less than Lode would, which Lode resents.

w: rainforest world with mountains and prairies
s: lush green and white clouds
lore: Alma's pharmaceutical forest: half the plants in Alma's medicines were first found here, and every plant found since is patented before it is named.

w: gas giant; Praevisio's white clinic platforms hold station at the breathable layer
s: dark green and pale grey bands, fine and even
pop: 3.4 billion hands on the clinic platforms
lore: Praevisio's white clinic platforms hold their place at the breathable layer to the metre, engines running day and night. Here Praevisio fits the white neural link on the left temple. Staff-grade hands queue for weeks, because no one is promoted without one.

w: gas giant of wildly changing weather
s: green and grey bands torn by shifting storms
m: three moons, all dark ice-rock, with the technicians' domes
pop: 2 million Staff technicians on the moons and in drifting instrument towers
lore: The weather changes by the hour, so Praevisio tests its forecasts here: technicians in domes on the three moons fly down to instrument towers drifting in the storms. It publishes its accuracy every quarter, and the figure has never been below ninety-nine percent.

w: gas giant; harbour towns on its big sea moon
s: a pale blue-white giant with three bright moons
m: three moons: a big living sea moon with white coasts, a smooth ice moon and a frozen-plains moon
lore: Harbour towns line the white coasts of the giant's sea moon, the brightest of its three lamps. Its harbour masters still issue Republic-era licences. Alma tolerates the moon as a heritage destination and sells tours of it.

w: glacier world; growers are widening the warm volcanic rift valleys
s: white ice cut by green rifts and patches of open water
m: three moons: one volcanic and two cratered rock
lore: Hot volcanic rifts under the glaciers grow vine-coffee and silk, and every year the growers melt the ice walls back a little further. They sell to Alma's resorts and are paid in the happiness pill as often as in cash.

w: temperate world of jungle and mountains
s: green and white, clinic towers on every coast
lore: Alma's largest birth holding outside Charter. One in nine hands born in the outer rim carries Cunabula's code in their Hand number, and the interest starts at the first breath.

w: temperate world, training grounds
s: grey and green with grid camps
lore: Continuity trains its Pacifiers here, rehearsing riots on a full-size copy of a Hand city. The rioters are Indentured hands, paid by the day.

w: temperate forested world
s: green forest and red roofs
lore: A small world that makes everything by hand and refuses machine-made goods. Hand traders sell it fake hand-made stock, and that is how the forgery charges started.

w: dry airless rocky world stacked with container fields
s: red-grey with container fields
lore: Lode's freight sorting holding on the trade route, a dead red rock where containers are stacked to the horizon. The night shift sleeps in the empty ones, pressurised by the hour.

w: frozen world of ice and rock
s: white and black, scarred by open pits
pop: 60,000 free miners, in the heated drifts of the mine
lore: Free miners took over a frozen chromite mine when Lode abandoned it, and live down in its heated drifts. They now sell the ore themselves. Lode wants it back, and the miners have mined the pass.

w: swamp world half drained, being flooded back
s: dry brown flats giving way to green wetland and new open water
lore: Lode drained these swamps for peat; the Growers are flooding them back, one dam at a time, and the green now reaches a third of the old wetland. A small Kiru exile camp shares the work.

w: hot ash world, glassed plains and live volcanoes
s: black with orange cracks and grey storms
lore: A forest world burned in the Republic's last war, its plains fused to black glass and its volcanoes woken. Eighteen thousand prospectors crack the glass for metal seams from sealed crawler camps, and the water shipped in costs more than the metal.

w: volcanic world being farmed green: ash terraces between live lava flows
s: grey ash and black flows with spreading green farms, red glow on the night side
lore: Every family owns a share in the volcanoes and farms the fresh ash on their slopes until the grey turns green; the fields now cover the old flows of half a continent. When a volcano erupts, the lost shares are redrawn by lot, and nobody has ever won one twice.

w: cold gas giant where two lanes end; its people drift in the clouds on rafts of old hulls
s: steel-blue and slate bands, two lit yard moons
m: two moons, both cut into refit yards
pop: 200 million, on hull rafts and the yard moons
lore: Where two great lanes end: the Runners' hub, and the Collective's main refit yard cut into both moons. Below, people live on gutted hulls lashed under gas bags, drifting wherever the wind goes. The Hand's maps call it a receivables district: everyone here owes money the Hand has stopped collecting, for now.

w: cold dark world of ice and rock, with one sheltered valley warmed by hot springs
s: dark blue-grey ice with one bright valley
pop: 600,000, nearly all in the valley town
lore: A free house where anyone can go dry, from either side, no questions asked, in the one valley that hot springs keep warm enough to live in. A handful of Ilmar volunteers run the night wards.

w: ochre gas giant; its large inner moon is a living jungle world
s: an ochre and rust banded giant with a dark green moon
m: three moons: a living jungle moon, and two outer moons held by Lode, one a timber mill
r: hardwood and resin from the jungle moon, fuel gas
pop: 30 million, in jungle towns on the living moon
lore: Lode holds the logging contract and the two outer moons, where its crews mill the timber; the jungle towns hold the ground of the living moon. Every tree cut is a small war.

w: humid swamp world
s: yellow-green swamp under heavy haze
lore: Worker cooperatives in stilt towns refine swamp plastics and sell to both sides. The Collective's fighter canopies are made from them.

w: cold pale gas giant on the Trunk Line, with an old customs hulk parked in low orbit
s: pale blue-grey bands with one bright hulk in low orbit
m: one, and not a natural one: the old customs hulk, a bright speck of plating in low orbit
lore: Settlers live in an old Republic customs hulk parked low over a gas giant on the Trunk Line, skimming fuel for passing ships, and still stamp passports that nobody needs.

w: ocean world, deep seas, almost no land
s: deep blue dotted with rig lights
lore: An ocean world of deep-sea oil rigs left by a company that went bankrupt before the Receivership. The rig crews' descendants still pump the oil, refine it on deck and sell it to anyone who docks.

w: tan and sage gas giant; its airfields are long platforms that ride inside the storm bands
s: tan and pale green bands torn by several rust-red storms
pop: about 1 million, a tenth of them students
lore: A flight school on runway platforms that ride the storm bands, where retired Runner pilots teach anyone who pays, Hand deserters included, to fly through shear that would tear a drone apart. Its graduates fly for every side, and the instructors make a point of never asking which.

w: desert world locked to its star; a pale gold twilight band, a glaring day side, a black night side
s: pale gold desert band between a white-hot face and a dark one with faint lights
m: three moons: a cratered rock, a frozen-plains moon and a captured lump
lore: Three million people who trade nothing and import nothing, living in the twilight and leaving the glare to the sand. No ship may land. Traders who have orbited it report lights in patterns on the night side, where nobody should live, and every year the patterns change.

w: tropical valley world, every valley dammed
s: green valleys and blue lakes under heavy cloud
lore: Every valley has a dam and a feud. The Hand settles water disputes for a fee and keeps them going.

w: forest and jungle world
s: deep green moss and forest under wet cloud
lore: A forest world carpeted in moss a metre deep that holds water like a sponge. The settlers sell the moss to desert worlds as soil, and Lode is lobbying to have the old forest treaty declared legacy.

w: double planet: two barren airless rocks circling each other, both domed
s: twin tan-gold worlds, the smaller one hanging close beside the larger
m: its twin (drawn as a big moon) and four small captured moons
pop: 50 million under domes on both worlds
lore: Two airless worlds circling each other, settled under domes by rival states who can see each other's lights all night. Each pays Runners to raid the other's ore.

w: world locked to its star: mesas, forest and desert along the twilight band, a desert day side, a cold night side
s: green and gold mesas in a ring of dusk, a glaring face and a dark one
lore: A free relay station whose dishes stand on the twilight mesas, fed by solar fields on the day side and cooled on the night side. It carries every signal it is paid to carry, Collective pirate broadcasts included. Alma has twice bought its debt to shut it down; twice the crews paid it off with one month of pirate fees.

w: airless rocky world; the docks are dug into crater walls under pressure halls
s: grey rock with dock lights along the crater rims
lore: Free repair docks cut into the crater walls, where Mordant's rivals refit freighters in airless bays and the crews live in pressure halls behind them. Walkouts work here under false names, and Mordant wants it shut.

w: forest and ocean world, wooded islands in a cool sea
s: green forested islands and blue seas
lore: A quiet coast where Runners who live to old age retire. Every porch has a rocking chair and a rifle, and the Repossessors who came looking for old debts are buried along the shore.

w: dry tawny plains of thin grass and high dark mountains
s: tawny gold plains broken by dark mountain spines
pop: 6 million herders in about forty clans
lore: Herder clans on the dry high plains settle every dispute by a three-day cattle drive: the first herd to reach the summit wins. Lode once offered to buy the grazing outright; the clans drove its surveyors' vehicles off a cliff, one per day.

w: dry rocky world of brick-red bluffs over thin brown rivers
s: brick-red bluffs along dark brown river valleys, little cloud
m: two small moons: a cratered rock and a captured lump
lore: The founders' law says every adult keeps a rifle, and the town buys more guns than it has people. Half the arms Runners carry into the Rim pass through its market, and Collective cells shop there more often than the elders admit.

w: temperate mountain world, terraced valleys and dense cities
s: green terraces and silver city lights in every valley
r: computers, robots, precision machinery; imports food and medicine
lore: Eight billion free citizens build the best thinking machines outside Hand space, and their charter forbids any of them to make a forecast. Praevisio has bid for the world eleven times. The Unwritten burned a factory here last year anyway.

w: hot arid world of desert hills, red mud plains and caves
s: rust-red flats streaked with dried riverbeds
r: people sold as contract labour, clay, cave salts
pop: 5 million, ruled by a dozen broker families
lore: The mud-plain families sell their own debtors to Hand labour brokers, a head at a time, and call it settling accounts. It is a free world that trades in the one thing the Hand would otherwise have to breed.

w: cool rocky world locked to its star; cave-riddled highlands along the twilight band
s: dusky violet twilight with pale dust storms, a dim face and a dark one
lore: In deep caves under the twilight highlands each family weaves one tapestry over a lifetime, knotting in every name it has lost; dyes dry in the glare of the day side, wool keeps in the night side's cold. Alma buys the finished pieces for executive resorts, never asking whose names hang on its walls.

w: dry canyon world, wind-cut gorges
s: ochre and burnt orange, veined with dark ravines
lore: Its canyon towns hang from the walls above a maze of gorges no drone has mapped twice. Dust pilots earn their name here by running the Narrows at night with their lights off; the canyon floor keeps the ones who fail.

w: wet temperate marsh world, peat bogs and reed plains
s: dull brown and olive under low cloud
m: two moons: a cratered rock and a dark ice-rock
lore: A billion peat cutters live on the marsh, and their council signed a fuel contract with Lode forty years ago to see out a famine. Every renewal gave Lode a little more of the bog, and in some years Lode's managers run the council outright.

w: airless blue-grey rocky world; one great port city roofed over a giant crater
s: blue-grey rock with a single bright crater sprawl
pop: 4 million dock families under the crater roof
lore: A free port roofed over a giant crater, where no hold is ever opened. The harbourmaster is the oldest dockhand still working, and nobody has dared ask the current one her age. Cargo passes through unrecorded, which is the whole business.

w: hot forest world, mountains and resin woods
s: deep green with amber-streaked slopes
lore: Resin forests where every tree is tapped by a named family, some for three hundred years. The resin seals half the hulls in the rim, and Mordant pays a year in advance, which means Mordant owns most of next year's sap.

w: airless rocky world, scrapfields on every plain
s: patchwork of grey wreck fields and dark hills, a ring of dumped hulls in low orbit
m: no moons; a ring of dumped hulls in low orbit
r: salvage, refitted ships, tractor gear, scrap metal
lore: Mordant pays to dump its scrapped hulls here and never asks where they go. The Walkouts live in pressure domes welded from old hull plate, strip every wreck and send it back out as a fighter, often with its registry number still visible under the new paint.

w: temperate plains world, foundry cities
s: orange city glow over flat tan plains
lore: Six billion foundry hands struck nineteen years ago, and Mordant answered by sealing the system off. The foundries never stopped: the strike committees run them still, and sell ingots to anyone who can slip the embargo.

w: temperate ocean world, scattered islands
s: deep blue with white island chains
lore: An ocean world of fishing families who give birth at sea, far from any registry. Their children have no Hand number and no Birth Debt; Alma calls them unregistered and keeps sending clinic ships that nobody boards.

w: cold rocky world, frozen pits and tundra
s: pale grey-white with dark mine scars
r: heavy metals, radioactive fuel; imports food
lore: Family claims dig uranium and heavy metals from frozen pits and sell to whoever pays most, Lode included. Miners rarely live past forty, but the families own their pits, and they never let you forget it.

w: warm dry world, salt flats and grassy plains
s: blinding white flats ringed with yellow grass
lore: When its nine moons line up, every forty years, brine floods the salt flats and every debt between families is cancelled. The next flood is due this year, and some creditors have quietly left.

w: hot storm world, flooded basalt plains under endless lightning
s: slate grey cloud lit by constant white flashes
pop: no one on the surface; about 200 Unwritten hermits on the moon
lore: Lightning never stops here; every beacon dropped on the surface burns out within the hour. The Hand's survey filed it as no yield, no approach. Two hundred Unwritten hermits live in the caves of its moon, because no machine can work in the storm below, and they count that a blessing.

w: moist temperate world, plains stripped of topsoil and regrowing in patches
s: patchy green over bare brown earth
pop: 1.2 million Growers and a few hundred Kiru exiles
lore: Growers replant plains Lode stripped for topsoil, one seed bed at a time. They use Lode's old survey stakes, still stamped EXHAUSTED, as fence posts. A small Kiru exile community farms beside them, and keeps apart.

w: warm swamp world, fog and black water
s: murky green under thick fog
lore: Runners sink their ships in the swamp whenever a Speculator passes, then raise them again on float bags. Every family here owns a hull it swears it found.

w: dry windswept world of high plateaus, its managed climate collapsed
s: pale tan with long dust streaks, a thin ring of satellite wreckage
m: two small moons, and a thin ring of wrecked weather satellites
lore: Unwritten pilgrims came here to live without machines and smashed the world's weather satellites in their first year; the wreckage still circles the planet. The managed climate collapsed, and the harvests have failed three times since. They call it a test of faith.

w: frigid ice world, glaciers over a frozen forest
s: brilliant white with blue glacier seams and a faint ring of debris
m: none; a faint ring of debris
lore: Under its glaciers stands a forest frozen solid for ten thousand years. Each summer cutting crews come out past the charts, live in heated sheds on the ice and saw it out, and Board families pay more for one table of glasswood than a Contract hand earns in a lifetime.

w: cold ice-locked world; the cities are buried under the ice
s: flat dull white with faint city warmth at the poles
m: three moons: two cratered rocks and a small captured rock
r: information, archives; imports food and technology
lore: Settlers who fled the Receivership built cities under the ice, warmed by deep vents at the poles, and brought a full copy of the old Republic's land registry: every deed from before the Hand. They sell extracts to anyone who asks. The Board would pay anything to see it burn.
